  47def read_molecules_from_file(
  48    input: str,
  49    key: str | None=None,
  50) -> Tuple[List[str], List[Dict[str, float]], List[str]]:
  51
  52    if input.endswith('.json'):
  53        data = read_json(input)
  54
  55    elif input.endswith('.yaml') or input.endswith('.yml'):
  56        import yaml
  57        with open(input, 'r') as f:
  58            data = yaml.load(f, Loader=yaml.FullLoader)
  59
  60    else:
  61        raise ValueError("Input file must be JSON or YAML format.")
  62
  63    if key is not None:
  64        data = data[key]
  65
  66    molecules = [_pt["molecule"] for _pt in data]
  67    extra_attrs = []
  68    extra_keys = sorted(list(set(data[0].keys()) - {"molecule"}))
  69    for k in extra_keys:
  70        extra_attrs.append({_pt["molecule"]: _pt[k] for _pt in data})
  71
  72    for m in molecules:
  73        match = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m)
  74        if match is None or len(match.groups()) != 3:
  75            raise ValueError(
  76                f"Invalid molecule name format: {m}."\
  77                f"Expected formats: {", ".join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
  78            )
  79
  80    return molecules, extra_attrs, extra_keys
  81
  82def read_molecule_pairs_from_file(input: str, key: str | None=None) ->List[tuple]:
  83    """ Extract molecule pairs from a json file.
  84
  85    A molcule refers to a specific copy of the modeled protein. e.g. DSC2a_0.
  86    The molecule pairs should be specified as follows:
  87
  88    [
  89        ["MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND", "MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"],
  90        ["MOL3_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND", "MOL4_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"],
  91        ...
  92    ]
  93
  94    ## Arguments:
  95
  96    - **input (str)**:<br />
  97        Path to the JSON file containing the molecule pairs.
  98
  99    ## Returns:
 100
 101    - **list**:<br />
 102        A list of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format
 103        (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
 104    """
 105
 106    if input.endswith('.json'):
 107        data = read_json(input)
 108        if key is not None:
 109            data = data[key]
 110    elif input.endswith('.yaml') or input.endswith('.yml'):
 111        import yaml
 112        with open(input, 'r') as f:
 113            data = yaml.load(f, Loader=yaml.FullLoader)
 114            if key is not None:
 115                data = data[key]
 116    else:
 117        raise ValueError("Input file must be JSON or YAML format.")
 118
 119    mol_pairs = [(_pt["molecule1"], _pt["molecule2"]) for _pt in data]
 120    extra_attrs = []
 121    extra_keys = list(set(data[0].keys()) - {"molecule1", "molecule2"})
 122    for k in extra_keys:
 123        extra_attrs.append({
 124            (_pt["molecule1"], _pt["molecule2"]): _pt[k] for _pt in data
 125        })
 126
 127    for m1, m2 in mol_pairs:
 128        match1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1)
 129        match2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2)
 130        if match1 is None or len(match1.groups()) != 3:
 131            raise ValueError(
 132                f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {m1}. "\
 133                f"Expected format is one of: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
 134            )
 135
 136        if match2 is None or len(match2.groups()) != 3:
 137            raise ValueError(
 138                f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {m2}. "\
 139                f"Expected format is one of: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
 140            )
 141
 142    return mol_pairs, extra_attrs, extra_keys

 144class Molecules:
 145
 146    def __init__(
 147        self,
 148        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
 149        input: str | None = None,
 150    ):
 151
 152        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
 153        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
 154        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
 155
 156        if isinstance(input, str):

 158                self.molecules,

 162            # print(self.molecules)
 163            # print(self.extra_attrs)
 164            # print(self.extra_attrs_keys)

 166            self.molecules = sorted(self.unique_mols)
 167
 168    def process_molecules(self, filter_by: list = []) -> List[str]:
 169
 170        self.enrich_molecules()
 171        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
 172            self.enrich_attributes()
 173
 174        if len(filter_by) > 0:
 175            self.filter_molecules(
 176                filter_by=filter_by,
 177                filter_level="copy",
 178            )
 179
 180        return self.molecules
 181
 182    def filter_molecules(self, filter_by: list, filter_level: str = "copy",) -> None:
 183
 184        assert filter_level in ["copy", "base"], "filter_level must be either 'copy' or 'base'"
 185
 186        _filter = {"copy": False, "base": True}
 187
 188        _filtered = [
 189            XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m, _filter[filter_level]) for m in filter_by
 190        ]
 191
 192        self.molecules = sorted(set([
 193            m for m in self.molecules
 194            if (
 195                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m, _filter[filter_level]) in _filtered
 196            )
 197        ]))
 198
 199        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
 200            self.extra_attrs = [
 201                {m: attr[m] for m in self.molecules if m in attr}
 202                for attr in self.extra_attrs
 203            ]
 204            self.extra_attrs = [
 205                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
 206                for attr in self.extra_attrs
 207            ]
 208
 209    def enrich_molecules(self) -> List[str]:
 210
 211        enriched_molecules = []
 212        for m in self.molecules:
 213            _enriched = self.enrich_molecule(m, fix_range=True)
 214            enriched_molecules.extend(_enriched)
 215
 216        self.molecules = sorted(set(enriched_molecules))
 217
 218    def enrich_attributes(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
 219
 220        enriched_attrs = []
 221
 222        for attr in self.extra_attrs:
 223            enriched_attr = {
 224                en_m: val for m, val in attr.items()
 225                for en_m in self.enrich_molecule(m, fix_range=True)
 226            }
 227            enriched_attrs.append(enriched_attr)
 228
 229        # sorted by molecule name
 230        self.extra_attrs = [
 231            dict(sorted(enriched_attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
 232            for enriched_attr in enriched_attrs
 233        ]
 234
 235    def raise_invalid_range_error(self, mol, specified_range):
 236
 237        valid_range = set(self.molwise_residues[mol])
 238        specified_range_set = set(get_res_range_from_key(specified_range))
 239
 240        if not specified_range_set.issubset(valid_range):
 241            raise ValueError(
 242                f"{mol}:{specified_range} is invalid. "\
 243                f"Valid residues - {mol}:{get_key_from_res_range(valid_range)}"
 244            )
 245
 246    @property
 247    def _enricher(self):
 248        return {
 249            True: lambda m, sel: f"{m}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{sel}",
 250            False: lambda m, sel: (
 251                f"{m}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}"
 252                f"{get_key_from_res_range(self.molwise_residues[m])}"
 253            ),
 254        }
 255
 256    @property
 257    def _range_checker(self):
 258        return {
 259            True: self.raise_invalid_range_error,
 260            False: lambda mol, specified_range: None,
 261        }
 262
 263    def enrich_molecule(self, m, fix_range: bool = False) -> List[str]:
 264
 265        enriched_molecules = []
 266
 267        try:
 268            base, cp_idx, sel = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m).groups()
 269
 270        except Exception as e:
 271            raise ValueError(
 272                f"Invalid format for molecule: {m}. "\
 273                f"Expected formats: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
 274            ) from e
 275
 276        copies_m = self.xyzr_parser.get_verify_copies(
 277            mol_basename=base,
 278            copy_idx=cp_idx,
 279        )
 280
 281        for cpy in copies_m:
 282
 283            condition = sel is not None and sel != ""
 284            if fix_range:
 285                valid_range = set(self.molwise_residues[cpy])
 286                specified_range_set = set(get_res_range_from_key(sel))
 287                common_range = valid_range.intersection(specified_range_set)
 288                common_range_key = get_key_from_res_range(common_range)
 289            else:
 290                self._range_checker[condition](cpy, sel)
 291                common_range_key = sel
 292            enriched_molecules.append(self._enricher[condition](cpy, common_range_key))
 293
 294        return enriched_molecules
 295
 296class MoleculePairs:
 297    """ Class to handle molecule pair data during interaction map generation."""
 298
 299    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
 300    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
 301
 302    molwise_residues: Dict[str, list]
 303    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to sets of residue numbers. Format: {
 304        "MOL1_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
 305        "MOL2_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
 306        ...
 307    } """
 308
 309    self_interaction: str
 310    """ String indicating how to handle self-interactions. Should be one of:
 311    - "allow_all": allow interactions between all molecule pairs, including
 312                   self-pairs and copy pairs.
 313    - "allow_none": disallow interactions between any molecule pairs of the same
 314                    molecule, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
 315    - "allow_copies": allow interactions between different copies of the same
 316                      molecule, but disallow self-pairs. (default)
 317    """
 318
 319    unique_mols: set
 320    """ Set of unique molecule names (without copy index) present in the model. """
 321
 322    mol_pairs: list
 323    """ List of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format
 324    (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
 325    This list is processed and enriched based on the specified molecule pairs"""
 326
 327    def __init__(
 328        self,
 329        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
 330        input: str | None = None,
 331        self_interaction: str = "allow_copies",
 332    ):
 333
 334        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
 335        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
 336        self.self_interaction = self_interaction
 337        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
 338        self.molecule_handler = Molecules(xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser)
 339
 340        if isinstance(input, str):
 341            (
 342                self.mol_pairs,
 343                self.extra_attrs,
 344                self.extra_attrs_keys,
 345            ) = read_molecule_pairs_from_file(input=input)
 346        else:
 347            self.mol_pairs = list(
 348                combinations_with_replacement(sorted(self.unique_mols), 2)
 349            )
 350
 351    @staticmethod
 352    def get_grouped_mol_pairs(mol_pairs: list) -> Dict[str, set]:
 353        """ Group molecule pairs by their base molecule names and residuerange,
 354        ignoring copy indices.
 355
 356        ## Arguments:
 357
 358        - **mol_pairs (list)**:<br />
 359            A list of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format
 360            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
 361
 362        ## Returns:
 363
 364        - **dict**:<br />
 365            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (without copy indices) to
 366            sets of molecule pairs (with copy indices) that belong to that pair
 367            name. The keys of the dictionary are in the format:
 368            "MOL1:RESSTART-RESEND:MOL2:RESSTART-RESEND" and the values are sets
 369            of tuples in the format:
 370            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
 371        """
 372
 373        grouped_mol_pairs = defaultdict(set)
 374
 375        for m1, m2 in mol_pairs:
 376            base1, _, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1).groups()
 377            base2, _, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2).groups()
 378            pair_name = (
 379                f"{base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
 380                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
 381                f"{base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
 382            )
 383            grouped_mol_pairs[pair_name].add((m1, m2))
 384
 385        return grouped_mol_pairs
 386
 387    def process_molecule_pairs(self, filter_by: list = []) -> List[tuple]:
 388        """ Process and enrich molecule pairs.
 389
 390        - Add copy indices and residue ranges.
 391        - Filter by specified molecule pairs if filter_by is not empty.
 392
 393        ## Arguments:
 394
 395        - **filter_by (list, optional):**:<br />
 396            A list of tuples specifying molecule pairs to filter by. Each tuple
 397            should be in the format:
 398            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND) where,
 399            COPYIDX and RESSTART-RESEND are be optional.
 400
 401        ## Returns:
 402
 403        - **list**:<br />
 404            A list of tuples containing the processed molecule pairs in the format
 405            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
 406        """
 407
 408        self._enrich_mol_pairs()
 409        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
 410            self._enrich_attributes()
 411
 412        self._filter_self_pairs()
 413
 414        if len(filter_by) > 0:
 415            self._filter_mol_pairs(
 416                filter_by=filter_by,
 417                filter_level="copy",
 418            )
 419
 420        return self.mol_pairs
 421
 422    def _enrich_mol_pairs(self) -> None:
 423        """ Enrich molecule pairs
 424
 425        - Add copy indices and residue ranges to the molecule pairs.
 426        """
 427
 428        enriched_mol_pairs = []
 429
 430        for m1, m2 in self.mol_pairs:
 431
 432            enriched_m1 = self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m1)
 433            enriched_m2 = self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m2)
 434
 435            for cpy1, cpy2 in product(enriched_m1, enriched_m2):
 436                enriched_mol_pairs.append((cpy1, cpy2))
 437
 438        self.mol_pairs = list(set(enriched_mol_pairs))
 439
 440    def _enrich_attributes(self) -> None:
 441
 442        enriched_attrs = []
 443
 444        for attr in self.extra_attrs:
 445            enriched_attr = {
 446                (en_m1, en_m2): val
 447                for (m1, m2), val in attr.items()
 448                for en_m1 in self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m1)
 449                for en_m2 in self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m2)
 450            }
 451            enriched_attrs.append(enriched_attr)
 452
 453        # sorted by molecule pair
 454        self.extra_attrs = [
 455            dict(sorted(enriched_attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
 456            for enriched_attr in enriched_attrs
 457        ]
 458
 459    def _filter_mol_pairs(
 460        self,
 461        filter_by: List[tuple],
 462        filter_level: str = "copy",
 463    ) -> None:
 464        """ Filter molecule pairs by specified molecule pairs.
 465
 466        ## Arguments:
 467
 468        - **filter_by (List[tuple])**:<br />
 469            A list of tuples specifying molecule pairs to filter by. Each tuple
 470            should be in the format:
 471            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND) where,
 472            COPYIDX and RESSTART-RESEND are be optional.
 473
 474        - **filter_level (str, optional):**:<br />
 475            The level at which to apply the filter. Should be either "copy" or "base".
 476            - "copy": filter by the full molecule pair names including copy indices
 477                      and residue ranges. (default)
 478            - "base": filter by the base molecule names only, ignoring copy indices
 479                      and residue ranges.
 480        """
 481
 482        assert filter_level in ["copy", "base"], "filter_level must be either 'copy' or 'base'"
 483
 484        _filter = {"copy": False, "base": True}
 485
 486        def get_mol_pair_names(pair):
 487            m1, m2 = pair
 488            return (
 489                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m1, _filter[filter_level]),
 490                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m2, _filter[filter_level])
 491            )
 492
 493        _filtered_mol_pairs = [
 494            (
 495                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m1, _filter[filter_level]),
 496                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m2, _filter[filter_level])
 497            )
 498            for m1, m2 in filter_by
 499        ]
 500
 501        self.mol_pairs = list(set([
 502            pair for pair in self.mol_pairs
 503            if (
 504                get_mol_pair_names(pair) in _filtered_mol_pairs or
 505                tuple(reversed(get_mol_pair_names(pair))) in _filtered_mol_pairs
 506            )
 507        ]))
 508
 509        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
 510            self.extra_attrs = [
 511                {
 512                    pair: attr[pair] for pair in self.mol_pairs if pair in attr
 513                }
 514                for attr in self.extra_attrs
 515            ]
 516            self.extra_attrs = [
 517                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
 518                for attr in self.extra_attrs
 519            ]
 520
 521    def _filter_self_pairs(self) -> None:
 522        """ Remove self-interactions based on self.self_interaction attribute."""
 523
 524        pairs_to_remove = set()
 525
 526        _do_dict = {
 527            "allow_all": lambda b1, c1, b2, c2: False,
 528            "allow_none": lambda b1, c1, b2, c2: b1 == b2,
 529            "allow_copies": lambda b1, c1, b2, c2: (b1 == b2) and (c1 == c2),
 530        }
 531
 532        for m1, m2 in self.mol_pairs:
 533
 534            base1, cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1).groups()
 535            base2, cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2).groups()
 536            assert (
 537                all([base1 is not None, base2 is not None]) and
 538                all([cp_idx1 is not None, cp_idx2 is not None])
 539            ), (
 540                f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {(m1, m2)}. "\
 541                "Expected format: MOL_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"
 542            )
 543
 544            if _do_dict[self.self_interaction](base1, cp_idx1, base2, cp_idx2):
 545                pairs_to_remove.add((m1, m2))
 546
 547        self.mol_pairs = [
 548            pair for pair in self.mol_pairs
 549            if pair not in pairs_to_remove
 550        ]
 551
 552        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
 553            self.extra_attrs = [
 554                {
 555                    pair: attr[pair] for pair in self.mol_pairs if pair in attr
 556                }
 557                for attr in self.extra_attrs
 558            ]
 559            self.extra_attrs = [
 560                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
 561                for attr in self.extra_attrs
 562            ]

 564def explode_map(
 565    q_map: np.ndarray,
 566    mol: str,
 567    molwise_xyzr_keys: Dict[str, list],
 568    by: str = "row",
 569) -> np.ndarray:
 570    """ Expand a bead-level distance/contact map to residue-level map along
 571    the specified axis.
 572
 573    ## Arguments:
 574
 575    - **q_map (np.ndarray)**:<br />
 576        The distance/contact map to be expanded.
 577
 578    - **mol (str)**:<br />
 579        The molecule name for which the map is being expanded (e.g. "MOL_COPYIDX").
 580
 581    - **by (str, optional):**:<br />
 582        The axis along which to expand the map. Should be either "row" or "col".
 583
 584    ## Returns:
 585
 586    - **np.ndarray**:<br />
 587        The expanded distance/contact map.
 588    """
 589
 590    assert q_map.ndim == 2, "q_map must be a 2D array."
 591
 592    repeat_ = {
 593        "row": lambda q, i: q[i, :],
 594        "col": lambda q, i: q[:, i],
 595    }
 596
 597    axis_ = {"row": 0, "col": 1}
 598
 599    special_keys = [
 600        (key.rsplit("_", 1)[1], idx)
 601        for idx, key in enumerate(molwise_xyzr_keys[mol])
 602        if "-" in key
 603    ]
 604    dup_attrs = []
 605
 606    for key, attr_idx in special_keys:
 607        num_repeats = len(get_res_range_from_key(key))
 608        to_add = np.tile(repeat_[by](q_map, attr_idx), (num_repeats - 1, 1))
 609        dup_attrs.append((to_add, attr_idx))
 610
 611    for to_add, attr_idx in reversed(dup_attrs):
 612        q_map = np.insert(q_map, attr_idx + 1, to_add, axis=axis_[by])
 613
 614    return q_map
 615
 616def expand_map_to_residue_level(
 617    q_map: np.ndarray,
 618    molwise_xyzr_keys: dict,
 619    pair_name: str,
 620) -> np.ndarray:
 621    """ Expand a bead-level distance/contact map to residue-level map.
 622
 623    ## Arguments:
 624
 625    - **q_map (np.ndarray)**:<br />
 626        Original distance/contact map.
 627
 628    - **pair_name (str)**:<br />
 629        The name of the molecule pair. (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
 630
 631    ## Returns:
 632
 633    - **np.ndarray**:<br />
 634        Expanded distance/contact map.
 635    """
 636
 637    _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
 638    base1, cp_idx1, _ = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
 639    base2, cp_idx2, _ = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
 640    mol1 = f"{base1}{MOL_COPY_SEP}{cp_idx1}"
 641    mol2 = f"{base2}{MOL_COPY_SEP}{cp_idx2}"
 642
 643    # expand the maps to include all residues in the selection
 644    q_map = explode_map(q_map, mol1, molwise_xyzr_keys, by="row")
 645    q_map = explode_map(q_map, mol2, molwise_xyzr_keys, by="col")
 646
 647    return q_map
 648
 649def get_binary_map(
 650    q_map: npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating],
 651    binarization_cutoff: float,
 652    map_type: str = "dmap",
 653    i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
 654) -> npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating]:
 655    """ Convert the distance or contact map to binary map based on cutoff.
 656
 657    ## Arguments:
 658
 659    - **q_map (npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating])**:<br />
 660        The distance or contact map to be binarized.
 661
 662    - **binarization_cutoff (float)**:<br />
 663        The cutoff value used for binarization.
 664        - For distance maps, this is the maximum distance for a pair to be
 665        considered in contact.
 666        - For contact maps, this is the minimum fraction of frames which should
 667        have the pair in contact for it to be considered a contact.
 668
 669    - **map_type (str, optional):**:<br />
 670        The type of map being binarized.
 671        Either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
 672
 673    - **i_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
 674        The integer data type to be used for the binary map.
 675
 676    ## Returns:
 677
 678    - **npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating]**:<br />
 679        The binary map.
 680    """
 681
 682    if map_type == "dmap":
 683        q_map[q_map < binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(1)
 684        q_map[q_map >= binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(0)
 685
 686    elif map_type == "cmap":
 687        q_map[q_map >= binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(1)
 688        q_map[q_map < binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(0)
 689
 690    q_map = q_map.astype(i_dtype)
 691
 692    return q_map
 693
 694def save_map_txt(
 695    q_map: npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating],
 696    save_dir: str,
 697    map_name: str,
 698    overwrite: bool = False
 699):
 700    """ Save a distance or contact map as a text file.
 701
 702    ## Arguments:
 703
 704    - **q_map (npt.NDArray[np.int_] | npt.NDArray[np.floating])**:<br />
 705        The distance or contact map to be saved as a text file.
 706
 707    - **save_dir (str)**:<br />
 708        The directory where the text file will be saved.
 709
 710    - **map_name (str)**:<br />
 711        The name of the map, which will be used as the filename (without extension).
 712
 713    - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
 714        Whether to overwrite the file if it already exists.
 715    """
 716
 717    save_path = os.path.join(save_dir, f"{map_name}.txt")
 718
 719    if not os.path.exists(save_path) or overwrite:
 720        np.savetxt(
 721            save_path,
 722            q_map,
 723            fmt="%.6f"
 724        )
 725
 726class PairwiseMaps:
 727    """ Class to handle pairwise distance and contact maps for given molecule pairs."""
 728
 729    mol_pairs: list
 730    """ List of enriched molecule pairs. See `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
 731
 732    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
 733    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
 734
 735    xyzr_mat: np.ndarray
 736    """ The raw XYZR data as a numpy array of shape (num_beads, num_frames, 4). """
 737
 738    xyzr_keys: list
 739    """ List of bead keys in the format "MOL_COPYIDX_RESNUM" or "MOL_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND",
 740    corresponding to the rows in xyzr_mat. """
 741
 742    molwise_residues: dict
 743    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to sets of residue numbers. Format: {
 744        "MOL1_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
 745        "MOL2_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
 746        ...
 747    } """
 748
 749    molwise_xyzr_keys: dict
 750    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of bead keys. Format: {
 751        "MOL1_COPYIDX": ["MOL1_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...],
 752        "MOL2_COPYIDX": ["MOL2_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...],
 753        ...
 754    } """
 755
 756    self_interaction: str
 757    """ String indicating how to handle self-interactions. Should be one of:
 758    - "allow_all": allow interactions between all molecule pairs, including
 759                   self-pairs and copy pairs.
 760    - "allow_none": disallow interactions between any molecule pairs of the same
 761                    molecule, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
 762    - "allow_copies": allow interactions between different copies of the same
 763                      molecule, but disallow self-pairs. (default)
 764    """
 765
 766    unique_mols: set
 767    """ Set of unique molecule names (without copy index) present in the model. """
 768
 769    f_dtype: np.dtype
 770    """ The floating point data type to use for the distance and contact maps. """
 771
 772    i_dtype: np.dtype
 773    """ The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps. """
 774
 775    contact_cutoff: float
 776    """ The cutoff distance used for binarization of the distance maps, which will be
 777    passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
 778    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
 779    """
 780
 781    fraction_cutoff: float
 782    """ The cutoff fraction used for binarization of the contact maps, which will
 783    be passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
 784    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
 785    """
 786
 787    def __init__(
 788        self,
 789        mol_pairs: list,
 790        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
 791        contact_cutoff: float,
 792        fraction_cutoff: float,
 793        self_interaction: bool = False,
 794        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
 795        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
 796    ):
 797
 798        self.mol_pairs = mol_pairs
 799        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
 800        self.xyzr_mat = xyzr_parser.xyzr_mat
 801        self.xyzr_keys = xyzr_parser.xyzr_keys
 802        self.num_frames = xyzr_parser.xyzr_mat.shape[1]
 803        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
 804        self.molwise_xyzr_keys = xyzr_parser.molwise_xyzr_keys
 805        self.self_interaction = self_interaction
 806        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
 807        self.f_dtype = f_dtype
 808        self.i_dtype = i_dtype
 809        self.contact_cutoff = contact_cutoff
 810        self.fraction_cutoff = fraction_cutoff
 811
 812    def process_pairwise_maps(
 813        self,
 814        pairwise_maps: dict,
 815        map_type: str,
 816        merge_operation: str = "average",
 817        merge_copies: bool = False,
 818        binarize_map: bool = False,
 819    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
 820        """ Process pairwise distance or contact maps by expanding to residue-level,
 821        merging across copies if specified, and binarizing if specified.
 822
 823        ## Arguments:
 824
 825        - **pairwise_maps (dict)**:<br />
 826            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
 827            to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 828
 829        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
 830            A string indicating the type of maps being processed.
 831            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
 832
 833        - **merge_copies (bool, optional):**:<br />
 834            Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the
 835            maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps
 836            will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the `merge_maps_by_copies`
 837            function. If False, the maps will be processed separately for each copy pair.
 838
 839        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
 840            Whether to binarize the maps based on the cutoff. If True, the maps will be
 841            converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a contact is
 842            defined as present if it is present in any of the copy pairs (if merge_copies
 843            is True) or based on the cutoff for each individual map (if merge_copies is False).
 844            If False, the maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values.
 845
 846        ## Returns:
 847
 848        - **dict**:<br />
 849            A dictionary of processed interaction maps per molecule pair.
 850        """
 851
 852        assert map_type in ["dmap", "cmap"], "map_type must be either 'dmap' or 'cmap'"
 853
 854        ############################################################################
 855        # Expand the maps to residue-level for plotting and patch extraction.
 856        ############################################################################
 857        for pair_name, pairwise_map in pairwise_maps.items():
 858
 859            pairwise_maps[pair_name] = expand_map_to_residue_level(
 860                q_map=pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype),
 861                molwise_xyzr_keys=self.molwise_xyzr_keys,
 862                pair_name=pair_name
 863            )
 864
 865        ############################################################################
 866        # Merge maps across copies if specified, and binarize if specified.
 867        ############################################################################
 868        if merge_copies:
 869
 870            pairwise_maps = self.merge_maps_by_copies(
 871                pairwise_maps=pairwise_maps,
 872                map_type=map_type,
 873                operation="or" if binarize_map else merge_operation,
 874                binarize_map=binarize_map,
 875            )
 876
 877        else:
 878
 879            for pair_name, pairwise_map in pairwise_maps.items():
 880
 881                if binarize_map:
 882                    pairwise_maps[pair_name] = get_binary_map(
 883                        q_map=pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype),
 884                        binarization_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff if map_type=="dmap" else self.fraction_cutoff,
 885                        map_type=map_type,
 886                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype
 887                    )
 888
 889                else:
 890                    pairwise_maps[pair_name] = pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype)
 891
 892        return pairwise_maps
 893
 894    def prepare_xyzr_batches(
 895        self,
 896        frame_batches: List[np.ndarray],
 897        res_range: Optional[str],
 898        mol_name: str
 899    ) -> Tuple[List[int], List[np.ndarray]]:
 900        """ Prepare batches of XYZR data for the specified molecule and residue range.
 901
 902        ## Arguments:
 903
 904        - **frame_batches (List[np.ndarray])**:<br />
 905            A list of numpy arrays, where each array contains the frame indices
 906            for a batch.
 907
 908        - **res_range (Optional[str])**:<br />
 909            A string specifying the residue range to select for the molecule.
 910            Should be in the format "RESSTART-RESEND". If None, all residues for
 911            the molecule will be selected.
 912
 913        - **mol_name (str)**:<br />
 914            The name of the molecule for which to prepare the XYZR batches. Should
 915            be in the format "MOL_COPYIDX".
 916
 917        ## Returns:
 918
 919        - **Tuple[List[int], List[np.ndarray]]**:<br />
 920            A tuple containing:
 921            - A list of indices corresponding to the selected residues for the
 922              molecule.
 923            - A list of numpy arrays, where each array contains the XYZR data
 924              for the selected residues and frames in the corresponding batch.
 925        """
 926
 927        res_range = (
 928            get_res_range_from_key(res_range)
 929            if res_range is not None else self.molwise_residues[mol_name]
 930        )
 931
 932        idx = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol_name, res_range, self.xyzr_keys)
 933        xyzr = self.xyzr_mat[idx, :, :].astype(self.f_dtype)
 934        xyzr_batches = [
 935            xyzr[:, f_batch, :].astype(self.f_dtype)
 936            for f_batch in frame_batches
 937        ]
 938
 939        del xyzr
 940
 941        return idx, xyzr_batches
 942
 943    def merge_maps_by_copies(
 944        self,
 945        pairwise_maps: dict,
 946        map_type: str,
 947        operation: str = "average",
 948        binarize_map:bool = False,
 949    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
 950        """ Merge contact or distance maps across copy pairs.
 951
 952        > [!NOTE]
 953        > if the binarize_map flag is set to True,
 954        > the merged map is a binary map where a contact is defined as present if
 955        > it is present in any of the copy pairs.
 956        >
 957        > if the binarize_map flag is set to False,
 958        > the merged map is - average of the distance/contact maps across copy pairs.
 959
 960        ## Arguments:
 961
 962        - **pairwise_maps (dict)**:<br />
 963            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
 964            to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 965
 966        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
 967            A string indicating the type of maps being merged.
 968            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
 969
 970        - **operation (str, optional):**:<br />
 971            The operation to use when merging the maps across copy pairs. Should be
 972            either "average" to take the average of the maps across copy pairs or "or"
 973            to take the logical OR of the maps across copy pairs when binarizing.
 974            (default: "average")
 975
 976        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
 977            Whether to binarize the merged maps based on the cutoff.
 978            - If True, the merged maps will be converted to binary maps using the
 979              `get_binary_map` function, where a contact is defined as present
 980               if it is present in any of the copy pairs.
 981            - If False, the merged maps will not be binarized and will retain
 982              their original values (e.g. average distances or contact frequencies).
 983              (default: False)
 984
 985        ## Returns:
 986
 987        - **dict**:<br />
 988            A dictionary mapping merged molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") to
 989            their corresponding merged distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 990        """
 991
 992        merged_pairwise_maps = defaultdict(list)
 993
 994        def raise_invalid_operation_error(operation):
 995            raise ValueError(f"Invalid operation: {operation}.")
 996
 997        func_ = {
 998            ("average", False): lambda v: np.mean(v, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
 999            ("or", True): lambda v: np.logical_or.reduce(v, axis=0).astype(self.i_dtype),
1000            ("min", False): lambda v: np.min(np.stack(v, axis=0), axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1001            ("max", False): lambda v: np.max(np.stack(v, axis=0), axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1002        }.get(
1003            (operation, binarize_map),
1004            lambda v: raise_invalid_operation_error(operation)
1005        )
1006
1007        for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
1008
1009            _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
1010            base1, _, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1011            base2, _, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1012
1013            merged_pair_name = (
1014                f"{base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
1015                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
1016                f"{base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
1017            )
1018
1019            _map = pairwise_maps[pair_name].copy()
1020
1021            if binarize_map is True:
1022                _map = get_binary_map(
1023                    q_map=_map,
1024                    binarization_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff if map_type=="dmap" else self.fraction_cutoff,
1025                    map_type=map_type,
1026                    i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1027                )
1028
1029            merged_pairwise_maps[merged_pair_name].append(_map)
1030
1031        merged_pairwise_maps = {
1032            k: func_(v)
1033            for k, v in merged_pairwise_maps.items()
1034        }
1035
1036        return merged_pairwise_maps
1037
1038    def fetch_pairwise_distances(
1039        self,
1040        output_dir: str,
1041        nproc: int,
1042        operation: str="min",
1043        subtract_radii: bool=True,
1044        overwrite: bool=False,
1045    ) -> dict:
1046        """ Fetch pairwise distance maps from XYZR data.
1047
1048        ## Arguments:
1049
1050        - **xyzr_mat (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1051            Array of shape (num_beads, num_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for all
1052            beads across all frames.
1053
1054        - **xyzr_keys (list)**:<br />
1055            List of strings representing the keys for each bead in the XYZR data.
1056            Each key should be formatted as "MoleculeName_CopyIndex_ResidueRangeStart-ResidueRangeEnd".
1057
1058        - **mol_pairs (list)**:<br />
1059            List of tuples, where each tuple contains two strings representing the
1060            names of the molecules in a binding pair, including copy indices and residue range information.
1061                For example:
1062            ```
1063            [
1064                ("ProteinA_copy1_10-50", "ProteinB_copy1_20-60"),
1065                ("ProteinA_copy2_10-50", "ProteinB_copy2_20-60"),
1066                ("ProteinC_copy1_5-30", "ProteinD_copy1_15-45"),
1067                ("ProteinC_copy2_5-30", "ProteinD_copy2_15-45")
1068            ]
1069            ```
1070
1071        - **output_dir (str)**:<br />
1072            Directory to save output distance map files. Each pairwise distance map will
1073            be saved as a text file named "Molecule1_Molecule2_dmap.txt" in this directory.
1074
1075        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1076            Number of processes to use for parallel distance map calculations.
1077
1078        - **f_dtype (np.dtype)**:<br />
1079            Float dtype for distance calculations.
1080
1081        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1082            Whether to overwrite existing distance map files. If False and a distance
1083            map file already exists for a given pair, the function will load the
1084            distance map from the file instead of recalculating it. Defaults to False.
1085
1086        ## Returns:
1087
1088        - **dict**:<br />
1089            Dictionary where keys are pair names formatted as "Molecule1_Molecule2" and
1090            values are arrays of shape (num_frames,) containing the minimum distance
1091            across all bead pairs for each frame.
1092        """
1093
1094        funcs = {
1095            "min": np.min,
1096            "average": np.average,
1097        }
1098
1099        pairwise_dmaps = {}
1100
1101        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), nproc)
1102
1103        for _m1, _m2 in tqdm.tqdm(self.mol_pairs):
1104
1105            _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1106            _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1107
1108            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
1109            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
1110            pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}" # this should include copy idx
1111
1112            dmap_txt = Path(output_dir) / f"{pair_name}_dmap.txt"
1113
1114            if os.path.exists(dmap_txt) and overwrite is False:
1115                pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(
1116                    dmap_txt,
1117                    dtype=self.f_dtype,
1118                )
1119                continue
1120
1121            _idx1, xyzr1_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1122                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1123                res_range=range1,
1124                mol_name=mol1,
1125            )
1126
1127            _idx2, xyzr2_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1128                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1129                res_range=range2,
1130                mol_name=mol2,
1131            )
1132
1133            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1134                futures = [
1135                    executor.submit(
1136                        PairwiseMaps.get_pairwise_distances,
1137                        xyzr1_b,
1138                        xyzr2_b,
1139                        self.f_dtype,
1140                        subtract_radii
1141                    )
1142                    for xyzr1_b, xyzr2_b in zip(xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches)
1143                ]
1144                results = []
1145                for future in tqdm.tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures)):
1146                    results.append(future.result())
1147
1148            del xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches
1149
1150            dmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros(self.num_frames, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1151
1152            n_frames = 0
1153            for i, flat_dmap_ in enumerate(results):
1154                # from each flattened dmap of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, batch_frames),
1155                # we take the minimum distance across all bead pairs for each frame,
1156                # resulting in an array of shape (batch_frames,)
1157                frame_slice = slice(n_frames, n_frames + flat_dmap_.shape[1])
1158                # dmap_m1_m2[frame_slice] = np.min(flat_dmap_, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype)
1159                dmap_m1_m2[frame_slice] = funcs[operation](flat_dmap_, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype)
1160                n_frames += flat_dmap_.shape[1]
1161
1162            del results
1163
1164            pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = dmap_m1_m2.astype(self.f_dtype)
1165
1166            if not os.path.exists(dmap_txt) or overwrite:
1167                np.savetxt(dmap_txt, dmap_m1_m2, fmt="%.6f")
1168
1169        return pairwise_dmaps
1170
1171    def fetch_pairwise_maps(
1172        self,
1173        interaction_map_dir: str,
1174        nproc: int,
1175        overwrite: bool = False,
1176    ) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
1177        """ Fetch pairwise distance and contact maps for specified molecule pairs.
1178
1179        > [!NOTE]
1180        > The selection defined in `mol_pairs` matters here.
1181        > The maps will only be computed for the selected residue ranges.
1182
1183        ## Arguments:
1184
1185        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
1186            The directory where interaction maps are saved.
1187
1188        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1189            The number of processes to use for parallel computation.
1190
1191        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1192            Whether to overwrite existing interaction map files. If False, function
1193            will load existing maps from disk if they are available, and skip
1194            recomputation. Note that the plots are always overwritten to reflect the
1195            current binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if
1196            the files already exist.
1197
1198        ## Returns:
1199
1200        - **tuple**:<br />
1201            A tuple containing two dictionaries:
1202            - pairwise_dmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2")
1203            to their corresponding average distance maps (numpy arrays).
1204            - pairwise_cmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their
1205            corresponding average contact maps (numpy arrays).
1206        """
1207
1208        pairwise_dmaps = {}
1209        pairwise_cmaps = {}
1210
1211        # num_frames = self.xyzr_mat.shape[1]
1212        num_beads = self.xyzr_mat.shape[0]
1213        assert self.xyzr_mat.shape[2] == 4, "Expected last dimension of xyzr_mat to be 4 (XYZR)."
1214        assert num_beads == len(self.xyzr_keys), "Number of beads in xyzr_mat does not match length of bead keys."
1215
1216        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), nproc)
1217
1218        for _m1, _m2 in tqdm.tqdm(self.mol_pairs):
1219
1220            pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}"
1221
1222            dmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_dmap.txt"
1223            cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_cmap.txt"
1224
1225            _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1226            _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1227
1228            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
1229            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
1230
1231            if (
1232                dmap_file.exists() and cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False
1233            ):
1234
1235                pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file)
1236                pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(dmap_file)
1237                continue
1238
1239            idx1, xyzr1_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1240                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1241                res_range=range1,
1242                mol_name=mol1,
1243            )
1244
1245            idx2, xyzr2_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1246                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1247                res_range=range2,
1248                mol_name=mol2,
1249            )
1250
1251            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1252                futures = [
1253                    executor.submit(
1254                        PairwiseMaps.get_pairwise_maps,
1255                        xyzr1_b,
1256                        xyzr2_b,
1257                        self.contact_cutoff,
1258                        self.f_dtype,
1259                        self.i_dtype
1260                    )
1261                    for xyzr1_b, xyzr2_b in zip(xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches)
1262                ]
1263                results = []
1264                for future in tqdm.tqdm(
1265                    as_completed(futures), total=len(futures)
1266                ):
1267                    results.append(future.result())
1268
1269            del xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches
1270
1271            dmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros((len(idx1), len(idx2)), dtype=self.f_dtype)
1272            cmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros((len(idx1), len(idx2)), dtype=self.i_dtype)
1273
1274            for i, (dmap_, cmap_) in enumerate(results):
1275                np.add(dmap_m1_m2, dmap_, out=dmap_m1_m2, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1276                np.add(cmap_m1_m2, cmap_, out=cmap_m1_m2, dtype=self.i_dtype)
1277
1278            del results
1279
1280            pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = (
1281                dmap_m1_m2.astype(self.f_dtype) / self.f_dtype(self.num_frames)
1282            )
1283            pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = (
1284                cmap_m1_m2.astype(self.i_dtype) / self.f_dtype(self.num_frames)
1285            )
1286
1287            save_map_txt(
1288                q_map=pairwise_dmaps[pair_name],
1289                save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1290                map_name=f"{pair_name}_dmap",
1291                overwrite=overwrite,
1292            )
1293
1294            save_map_txt(
1295                q_map=pairwise_cmaps[pair_name],
1296                save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1297                map_name=f"{pair_name}_cmap",
1298                overwrite=overwrite,
1299            )
1300
1301        del self.xyzr_mat
1302
1303        return pairwise_dmaps, pairwise_cmaps
1304
1305    @staticmethod
1306    def get_pairwise_distances(
1307        xyzr1: np.ndarray,
1308        xyzr2: np.ndarray,
1309        f_dtype: np.dtype=np.float64,
1310        subtract_radii: bool=True,
1311    ):
1312        """ Given two arrays of XYZR, return all pairwise distances.
1313
1314        ## Arguments:
1315
1316        - **xyzr1 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1317            Array of shape (n_beads1, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 1.
1318
1319        - **xyzr2 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1320            Array of shape (n_beads2, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 2.
1321
1322        - **f_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1323            Float dtype for distance calculations. Defaults to np.float64.
1324
1325        ## Returns:
1326
1327        - **np.ndarray**:<br />
1328            Array of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames) containing pairwise distances.
1329        """
1330
1331        coords1 = xyzr1[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1332        coords2 = xyzr2[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1333
1334        radii1 = xyzr1[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1335        radii2 = xyzr2[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1336
1337        n_frames = coords1.shape[1]
1338        n_beads1 = coords1.shape[0]
1339        n_beads2 = coords2.shape[0]
1340
1341        radii_sum = np.zeros((radii1.shape[0], radii2.shape[0]), dtype=f_dtype)
1342        np.add(
1343            radii1[:, None, 0].copy(),
1344            radii2[None, :, 0].copy(),
1345            out=radii_sum,
1346        )
1347
1348        flat_distances = np.zeros((n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames), dtype=f_dtype)
1349
1350        for i in range(n_frames):
1351
1352            temp_dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1353
1354            np.subtract(
1355                cdist(coords1[:, i, :], coords2[:, i, :]),
1356                radii_sum if subtract_radii else 0.0,
1357                out=temp_dmap,
1358                dtype=f_dtype,
1359            )
1360            temp_dmap[temp_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1361
1362            flat_distances[:, i] = temp_dmap.flatten().astype(f_dtype)
1363
1364            del temp_dmap
1365
1366        return flat_distances
1367
1368    @staticmethod
1369    def get_pairwise_maps(
1370        xyzr1: np.ndarray,
1371        xyzr2: np.ndarray,
1372        cutoff: float,
1373        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
1374        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
1375    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
1376        """ Compute pairwise distance and contact maps between two sets of beads
1377        over multiple frames.
1378
1379        NOTE: Pay attention to the size of the input arrays to avoid memory issues.
1380
1381        ## Arguments:
1382
1383        - **xyzr1 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1384            XYZR data for molecule 1, (n_beads1, n_frames, 4).
1385
1386        - **xyzr2 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1387            XYZR data for molecule 2, (n_beads2, n_frames, 4).
1388
1389        - **cutoff (float)**:<br />
1390            Distance cutoff for contact map.
1391
1392        - **f_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1393            Data type for distance map calculations.
1394
1395        - **i_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1396            Data type for contact map calculations.
1397
1398        ## Returns:
1399
1400        - **tuple**:<br />
1401            - **dmap (np.ndarray)**: Distance map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
1402            - **cmap (np.ndarray or None)**: Contact map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
1403        """
1404
1405        coords1 = xyzr1[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1406        coords2 = xyzr2[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1407
1408        radii1 = xyzr1[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1409        radii2 = xyzr2[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1410
1411        n_frames = coords1.shape[1]
1412        n_beads1 = coords1.shape[0]
1413        n_beads2 = coords2.shape[0]
1414
1415        radii_sum = np.zeros((radii1.shape[0], radii2.shape[0]), dtype=f_dtype)
1416        np.add(
1417            radii1[:, None, 0].copy(),
1418            radii2[None, :, 0].copy(),
1419            out=radii_sum,
1420        )
1421
1422        dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1423        cmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=i_dtype)
1424
1425        for i in range(n_frames):
1426
1427            temp_dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1428
1429            np.subtract(
1430                cdist(coords1[:, i, :], coords2[:, i, :]),
1431                radii_sum,
1432                out=temp_dmap,
1433                dtype=f_dtype,
1434            )
1435            temp_dmap[temp_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1436
1437            np.add(
1438                dmap,
1439                temp_dmap,
1440                out=dmap,
1441                dtype=f_dtype,
1442            )
1443
1444            temp_cmap = (temp_dmap <= cutoff).astype(i_dtype)
1445
1446            np.add(
1447                cmap,
1448                temp_cmap,
1449                out=cmap,
1450                dtype=i_dtype,
1451            )
1452
1453            del temp_dmap, temp_cmap
1454
1455        return dmap, cmap
1456
1457class PairwiseContactMaps:
1458
1459    mol_pairs: list
1460    """ List of enriched molecule pairs. See `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
1461
1462    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
1463    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
1464
1465    xyzr_mat: np.ndarray
1466    """ The raw XYZR data as a numpy array of shape (num_beads, num_frames, 4). """
1467
1468    xyzr_keys: list
1469    """ List of bead keys in the format "MOL_COPYIDX_RESNUM" or "MOL_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND",
1470    corresponding to the rows in xyzr_mat. """
1471
1472    molwise_residues: dict
1473    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to sets of residue numbers. Format: {
1474        "MOL1_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
1475        "MOL2_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
1476        ...
1477    } """
1478
1479    molwise_xyzr_keys: dict
1480    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of bead keys. Format: {
1481        "MOL1_COPYIDX": ["MOL1_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...],
1482        "MOL2_COPYIDX": ["MOL2_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...],
1483        ...
1484    } """
1485
1486    self_interaction: str
1487    """ String indicating how to handle self-interactions. Should be one of:
1488    - "allow_all": allow interactions between all molecule pairs, including
1489                   self-pairs and copy pairs.
1490    - "allow_none": disallow interactions between any molecule pairs of the same
1491                    molecule, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
1492    - "allow_copies": allow interactions between different copies of the same
1493                      molecule, but disallow self-pairs. (default)
1494    """
1495
1496    unique_mols: set
1497    """ Set of unique molecule names (without copy index) present in the model. """
1498
1499    f_dtype: np.dtype
1500    """ The floating point data type to use for the distance and contact maps. """
1501
1502    i_dtype: np.dtype
1503    """ The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps. """
1504
1505    contact_cutoff: float
1506    """ The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be
1507    passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
1508    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
1509    """
1510
1511    def __init__(
1512        self,
1513        mol_pairs: list,
1514        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
1515        cutoff: float,
1516        merge_copies: bool = False,
1517        self_interaction: bool = False,
1518        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
1519        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
1520    ):
1521
1522        self.mol_pairs = mol_pairs
1523        self.grouped_mol_pairs = MoleculePairs.get_grouped_mol_pairs(
1524            mol_pairs=self.mol_pairs
1525        )
1526        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
1527        self.xyzr_mat = xyzr_parser.xyzr_mat
1528        self.xyzr_keys = xyzr_parser.xyzr_keys
1529        self.num_frames = xyzr_parser.xyzr_mat.shape[1]
1530        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
1531        self.molwise_xyzr_keys = xyzr_parser.molwise_xyzr_keys
1532        self.merge_copies = merge_copies
1533        self.self_interaction = self_interaction
1534        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
1535        self.f_dtype = f_dtype
1536        self.i_dtype = i_dtype
1537        self.contact_cutoff = cutoff
1538        self.modelwise_cmaps = {}
1539
1540    @staticmethod
1541    def contact_map_worker(
1542        batch_xyz: np.ndarray,
1543        radii_sum: np.ndarray,
1544        contact_cutoff: float,
1545        grouped_mol_pairs: Dict[str, set],
1546        merge_copies: bool,
1547        f_dtype: np.dtype,
1548        i_dtype: np.dtype,
1549        molwise_xyzr_keys: dict,
1550        molwise_residues: dict,
1551        xyzr_keys: list,
1552    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
1553
1554        batchwise_cmaps = {}
1555
1556        for frame_id in range(batch_xyz.shape[1]):
1557            pairwise_cmaps = {}
1558            frame_coords = batch_xyz[:, frame_id, :].astype(f_dtype)
1559            diffs = pdist(frame_coords)
1560            frame_dmap = squareform(diffs, checks=False).astype(f_dtype)
1561            np.subtract(
1562                frame_dmap,
1563                radii_sum,
1564                out=frame_dmap,
1565                dtype=f_dtype,
1566            )
1567            frame_dmap[frame_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1568            frame_cmap = (frame_dmap <= contact_cutoff).astype(i_dtype)
1569
1570            for base_pair, copy_pairs in grouped_mol_pairs.items():
1571
1572                for _m1, _m2 in copy_pairs:
1573
1574                    pair_name, pair_cmap = PairwiseContactMaps.extract_copy_pair_contact_map(
1575                        frame_cmap=frame_cmap,
1576                        m1=_m1,
1577                        m2=_m2,
1578                        molwise_xyzr_keys=molwise_xyzr_keys,
1579                        molwise_residues=molwise_residues,
1580                        xyzr_keys=xyzr_keys,
1581                        merge_copies=merge_copies,
1582                    )
1583
1584                    if pair_name not in pairwise_cmaps:
1585                        cmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros_like(pair_cmap, dtype=i_dtype)
1586
1587                    np.logical_or(
1588                        pair_cmap,
1589                        cmap_m1_m2,
1590                        out=cmap_m1_m2,
1591                    )
1592                    pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = cmap_m1_m2
1593
1594                    if merge_copies is True:
1595                        continue
1596
1597                    PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1598                        cmaps_to_update=batchwise_cmaps,
1599                        cmaps_to_add=pairwise_cmaps,
1600                        pair_name=pair_name,
1601                        i_dtype=i_dtype,
1602                    )
1603
1604                if merge_copies is False:
1605                    continue
1606
1607                PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1608                    cmaps_to_update=batchwise_cmaps,
1609                    cmaps_to_add=pairwise_cmaps,
1610                    pair_name=base_pair,
1611                    i_dtype=i_dtype,
1612                )
1613
1614        return batchwise_cmaps
1615
1616    @staticmethod
1617    def update_cmaps(
1618        cmaps_to_update,
1619        cmaps_to_add,
1620        pair_name,
1621        i_dtype=np.int32,
1622    ):
1623
1624        if pair_name not in cmaps_to_update:
1625            cmaps_to_update[pair_name] = np.zeros_like(cmaps_to_add[pair_name], dtype=i_dtype)
1626
1627        np.add(
1628            cmaps_to_add[pair_name].astype(i_dtype),
1629            cmaps_to_update[pair_name].astype(i_dtype),
1630            out=cmaps_to_update[pair_name], dtype=i_dtype
1631        )
1632
1633    @staticmethod
1634    def extract_copy_pair_contact_map(
1635        frame_cmap,
1636        m1,
1637        m2,
1638        molwise_xyzr_keys,
1639        molwise_residues,
1640        xyzr_keys,
1641        merge_copies=False,
1642    ):
1643
1644        _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1).groups()
1645        _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2).groups()
1646
1647        pair_name = f"{m1}{PAIR_SEP}{m2}"
1648
1649        mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m1, only_base=False)
1650        mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m2, only_base=False)
1651
1652        res_range1 = (
1653            get_res_range_from_key(range1)
1654            if range1 is not None else molwise_residues[mol1]
1655        )
1656
1657        idx1 = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol1, res_range1, xyzr_keys)
1658
1659        res_range2 = (
1660            get_res_range_from_key(range2)
1661            if range2 is not None else molwise_residues[mol2]
1662        )
1663
1664        idx2 = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol2, res_range2, xyzr_keys)
1665
1666        pair_cmap = frame_cmap[np.ix_(idx1, idx2)]
1667        pair_cmap = expand_map_to_residue_level(
1668            q_map=pair_cmap,
1669            molwise_xyzr_keys=molwise_xyzr_keys,
1670            pair_name=pair_name,
1671        )
1672
1673        if merge_copies:
1674            pair_name = (
1675                f"{_base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
1676                PAIR_SEP +
1677                f"{_base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
1678            )
1679
1680        return pair_name, pair_cmap
1681
1682    def compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1683        self,
1684        nproc: int,
1685        interaction_map_dir: str,
1686        overwrite: bool = False,
1687    ) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
1688
1689        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), args.nproc)
1690
1691        radii_data = self.xyzr_mat[:, 0, 3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1692        radii_sum = np.zeros(
1693            (radii_data.shape[0], radii_data.shape[0]), dtype=self.f_dtype
1694        )
1695        np.add(
1696            radii_data[:, None].copy(),
1697            radii_data[None, :].copy(),
1698            out=radii_sum,
1699        )
1700
1701        xyz_data = self.xyzr_mat[:, :, :3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1702        batchwise_xyz = [
1703            xyz_data[:, frame_batch, :3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1704            for frame_batch in frame_batches
1705        ]
1706
1707        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1708            futures = [
1709                executor.submit(
1710                    PairwiseContactMaps.contact_map_worker,
1711                    batch_xyz=xyz_batch,
1712                    radii_sum=radii_sum,
1713                    contact_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff,
1714                    grouped_mol_pairs=self.grouped_mol_pairs,
1715                    merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1716                    f_dtype=self.f_dtype,
1717                    i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1718                    molwise_xyzr_keys=self.molwise_xyzr_keys,
1719                    molwise_residues=self.molwise_residues,
1720                    xyzr_keys=self.xyzr_keys,
1721                )
1722                for xyz_batch in batchwise_xyz
1723            ]
1724            for future in as_completed(futures):
1725
1726                batch_cmaps = future.result()
1727
1728                for pair_name in batch_cmaps.keys():
1729
1730                    PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1731                        cmaps_to_update=self.modelwise_cmaps,
1732                        cmaps_to_add=batch_cmaps,
1733                        pair_name=pair_name,
1734                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1735                    )
1736                    save_map_txt(
1737                        q_map=self.modelwise_cmaps[pair_name],
1738                        save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1739                        map_name=f"{pair_name}_cmap",
1740                        overwrite=overwrite,
1741                    )
1742
1743        self.modelwise_cmaps = {
1744            pair_name: cmap / self.num_frames
1745            for pair_name, cmap in self.modelwise_cmaps.items()
1746        }
1747
1748    def fetch_pairwise_contact_maps(
1749        self,
1750        interaction_map_dir: str,
1751        nproc: int,
1752        overwrite: bool = False,
1753    ) -> dict:
1754
1755        # try to load existing maps from disk if available and overwrite is False
1756        if self.merge_copies is True:
1757            for base_pair, copy_pairs in self.grouped_mol_pairs.items():
1758
1759                cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{base_pair}_cmap.txt"
1760                if cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False:
1761                    print(f"Loading existing contact map for {base_pair} from {cmap_file}.")
1762                    self.modelwise_cmaps[base_pair] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1763                else:
1764                    self.compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1765                        nproc=nproc,
1766                        interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1767                        overwrite=overwrite,
1768                    )
1769                    break
1770        else:
1771            for _m1, _m2 in self.mol_pairs:
1772
1773                pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}"
1774                cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_cmap.txt"
1775
1776                if cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False:
1777                    print(f"Loading existing contact map for {base_pair} from {cmap_file}.")
1778                    self.modelwise_cmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1779                else:
1780                    self.compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1781                        nproc=nproc,
1782                        interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1783                        overwrite=overwrite,
1784                    )
1785                    break
1786
1787        return self.modelwise_cmaps
1788
1789class Interaction:
1790    """ Class for computing interaction maps for selected molecule pairs."""
1791
1792    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
1793    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
1794
1795    molwise_residues: dict
1796    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of residue numbers. Format: {
1797        "MOL1": [residue numbers],
1798        "MOL2": [residue numbers],
1799        ...
1800    } """
1801
1802    contact_cutoff: float
1803    """ The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be
1804    passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
1805    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
1806    """
1807
1808    fraction_cutoff: float
1809    """ The cutoff for the fraction of frames in which a contact is present, used for
1810    binarization of the contact maps. This will be passed to the `get_binary_map`
1811    function if binarization of contact maps is specified. See :func:`get_binary_map`
1812    for more details.
1813    """
1814
1815    f_dtype: np.dtype
1816    """ The floating point data type to use for the distance/contact maps. """
1817
1818    i_dtype: np.dtype
1819    """ The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps. """
1820
1821    merge_copies: bool
1822    """ Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the
1823    maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps
1824    will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the `merge_maps_by_copies`
1825    function. If False, the maps will be treated separately for each copy pair.
1826    """
1827
1828    sel_mol_pairs: list
1829    """ List of selected molecule pairs based on the input selection. See
1830    `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
1831
1832    mol_pairs: list
1833    """ List of all molecule pairs. See `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
1834
1835    def __init__(
1836        self,
1837        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
1838        contact_cutoff: float,
1839        fraction_cutoff: float,
1840        input: str = None,
1841        merge_copies=False,
1842        self_interaction: str = "allow_none",
1843        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
1844        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
1845    ):
1846
1847        if not xyzr_parser.is_setup:
1848            xyzr_parser.parse_xyzr_h5_file()
1849
1850        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
1851        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
1852
1853        self.contact_cutoff = contact_cutoff
1854        self.fraction_cutoff = fraction_cutoff
1855        self.f_dtype = f_dtype
1856        self.i_dtype = i_dtype
1857        self.merge_copies = merge_copies
1858
1859        sel_mol_pair_handler = MoleculePairs(
1860            xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser,
1861            input=input,
1862            self_interaction=self_interaction,
1863        )
1864        mol_pair_handler = MoleculePairs(
1865            xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser,
1866            input=None,
1867            self_interaction=self_interaction,
1868        )
1869        sel_mol_pair_handler.process_molecule_pairs()
1870        self.sel_mol_pairs = sel_mol_pair_handler.mol_pairs
1871        mol_pair_handler.process_molecule_pairs(
1872            filter_by=self.sel_mol_pairs,
1873        )
1874        self.mol_pairs = mol_pair_handler.mol_pairs
1875
1876        # self.pairwise_maps_handler = PairwiseContactMaps(
1877        #     mol_pairs=self.mol_pairs,
1878        #     xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser,
1879        #     cutoff=cutoff,
1880        #     merge_copies=merge_copies,
1881        #     self_interaction=self_interaction,
1882        #     f_dtype=f_dtype,
1883        #     i_dtype=i_dtype,
1884        # )
1885
1886        self.pairwise_maps_handler = PairwiseMaps(
1887            mol_pairs=self.mol_pairs,
1888            xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser,
1889            contact_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff,
1890            fraction_cutoff=self.fraction_cutoff,
1891            self_interaction=self_interaction,
1892            f_dtype=f_dtype,
1893            i_dtype=i_dtype,
1894        )
1895
1896    def compute_interaction_maps(
1897        self,
1898        interaction_map_dir: str,
1899        nproc: int,
1900        overwrite: bool = False,
1901        binarize_dmap: bool = False,
1902        binarize_cmap: bool = False,
1903    ) -> None:
1904        """ Compute pairwise distance and contact maps for the selected molecule pairs.
1905
1906        ## Arguments:
1907
1908        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
1909            The directory where the computed interaction maps will be saved.
1910
1911        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1912            The number of processes to use for parallel computation of the maps.
1913
1914        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1915            Whether to overwrite existing map files in the interaction_map_dir. If False,
1916            the function will load existing maps from disk if they are available, and skip
1917            recomputation. Note that the plots are always overwritten to reflect the current
1918            binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if the files already exist.
1919
1920        - **binarize_dmap (bool, optional):**:<br />
1921            Whether to binarize the distance maps based on the cutoff. If True, the distance
1922            maps will be converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a
1923            contact is defined as present if the distance is less than or equal to the cutoff.
1924            If False, the distance maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values
1925            (e.g. average distances). (default: False)
1926
1927        - **binarize_cmap (bool, optional):**:<br />
1928            Whether to binarize the contact maps based on the cutoff. If True, the contact maps
1929            will be converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a contact
1930            is defined as present if the contact frequency is greater than or equal to the cutoff.
1931            If False, the contact maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values
1932            (e.g. average contact frequencies). (default: False)
1933        """
1934        (
1935            pairwise_dmaps,
1936            pairwise_cmaps
1937        ) = self.pairwise_maps_handler.fetch_pairwise_maps(
1938            interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1939            nproc=nproc,
1940            overwrite=overwrite,
1941        )
1942
1943        self.pairwise_dmaps = self.pairwise_maps_handler.process_pairwise_maps(
1944            pairwise_maps=pairwise_dmaps,
1945            map_type="dmap",
1946            merge_operation="average",
1947            merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1948            binarize_map=binarize_dmap,
1949        )
1950
1951        self.pairwise_cmaps = self.pairwise_maps_handler.process_pairwise_maps(
1952            pairwise_maps=pairwise_cmaps,
1953            map_type="cmap",
1954            merge_operation="max",
1955            merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1956            binarize_map=binarize_cmap,
1957        )
1958
1959        if self.merge_copies:
1960            self.xyzr_parser.merge_residue_selection_by_copies()
1961            self.molwise_residues = self.xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
1962
1963        self.map_slices = self.generate_map_slices(
1964            pairwise_keys=list(self.pairwise_dmaps.keys()),
1965        )
1966

1968    #     self,

1973

1975    #         interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,

1978    #     )
1979
