1982    #         self.molwise_residues = self.xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
1983
1984    #     self.map_slices = self.generate_map_slices(
1985    #         pairwise_keys=list(modelwise_cmaps.keys()),
1986    #     )
1987
1988    def generate_map_slices(
1989        self,
1990        pairwise_keys: list,
1991    ) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]]:
1992        """ Generate a dictionary of slice names and their corresponding residue
1993        ranges for each molecule pair.
1994
1995        ## Arguments:
1996
1997        - **pairwise_keys (list)**:<br />
1998            A list of molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") corresponding to the
1999            keys in the pairwise_maps dictionary. This is used to ensure that the
2000            generated slice names are consistent with the keys in the pairwise_maps
2001            dictionary, and to filter out any selected molecule pairs that do not have
2002            corresponding maps.
2003
2004        ## Returns:
2005
2006        - **dict**:<br />
2007            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to dictionaries of slice names and
2008            their corresponding residue ranges. Format:
2009            {
2010                "MOL1:MOL2": {
2011                    "slice_name1": {
2012                        "s1": start residue number for mol1,
2013                        "e1": end residue number for mol1,
2014                        "s2": start residue number for mol2,
2015                        "e2": end residue number for mol2,
2016                    },
2017                    "slice_name2": {
2018                        ...
2019                    },
2020                    ...
2021                },
2022                ...
2023            }
2024        """
2025
2026        map_slices = {k: {} for k in pairwise_keys}
2027
2028        for _m1, _m2 in self.sel_mol_pairs:
2029
2030            _base1, _cp_idx1, sel1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
2031            _base2, _cp_idx2, sel2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
2032
2033            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=self.merge_copies)
2034            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=self.merge_copies)
2035
2036            range1 = f"{min(self.molwise_residues[mol1])}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{max(self.molwise_residues[mol1])}"
2037            range2 = f"{min(self.molwise_residues[mol2])}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{max(self.molwise_residues[mol2])}"
2038
2039            pair_name = (
2040                f"{mol1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
2041                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2042                f"{mol2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
2043            )
2044
2045            if pair_name not in pairwise_keys:
2046                print(f"Warning: {pair_name} not found in computed maps. Skipping.")
2047                continue
2048
2049            s1, e1 = get_res_range_from_key(sel1)[0], get_res_range_from_key(sel1)[-1]
2050            s2, e2 = get_res_range_from_key(sel2)[0], get_res_range_from_key(sel2)[-1]
2051
2052            slice_name = (
2053                f"{mol1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{s1}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{e1}" +
2054                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2055                f"{mol2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{s2}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{e2}"
2056            )
2057
2058            map_slices[pair_name][slice_name] = {
2059                "s1": int(s1),
2060                "e1": int(e1),
2061                "s2": int(s2),
2062                "e2": int(e2),
2063            }
2064
2065        return map_slices
2066
2067    def save_output(
2068        self,
2069        pairwise_maps,
2070        interaction_map_dir,
2071        nproc,
2072        cutoff,
2073        binarize_map,
2074        map_type,
2075        output_type: str = "patches+plots",
2076        plotting_lib: str = "matplotlib",
2077    ):
2078        """ Save the processed interaction maps as plots and/or patches.
2079
2080        ## Arguments:
2081
2082        - **pairwise_maps (_type_)**:<br />
2083            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their corresponding distance
2084            or contact maps (numpy arrays).
2085
2086        - **interaction_map_dir (_type_)**:<br />
2087            The directory where the output maps and plots will be saved.
2088
2089        - **nproc (_type_)**:<br />
2090            The number of processes to use for parallel processing when saving the
2091            maps and plots.
2092
2093        - **cutoff (_type_)**:<br />
2094            The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be
2095            included in the plot title and colorbar label. See :func:`get_binary_map`
2096            for more details.
2097
2098        - **binarize_map (_type_)**:<br />
2099            Whether to binarize the maps before saving and plotting. If True, the maps
2100            will be converted to binary maps based on the cutoff value before saving
2101            and plotting.
2102
2103        - **map_type (_type_)**:<br />
2104            A string indicating the type of maps being saved and plotted.
2105            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
2106
2107        - **output_type (str, optional):**:<br />
2108            A string indicating the type of output to save. Can be either "patches",
2109            "plots", or "patches+plots".
2110            - If "patches", only the patches will be saved as csv files.
2111            - If "plots", only the plots will be saved as png files.
2112            - If "patches+plots", both the patches and plots will be saved.
2113
2114        - **plotting_lib (str, optional):**:<br />
2115            The plotting library to use for generating the plots. Can be either
2116            "matplotlib" or "plotly". Default is "matplotlib".
2117        """
2118
2119        output_types = output_type.split("+")
2120        assert all([ot in ["patches", "plots"] for ot in output_types]), (
2121            f"Invalid output_type: {output_type}. Expected 'patches', 'plots', or 'patches+plots'."
2122        )
2123        nproc = min(nproc, len(pairwise_maps), 20)
2124        executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc)
2125
2126        if "plots" in output_types:
2127            for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
2128                executor.submit(
2129                    Interaction.plot_map,
2130                    pairwise_maps[pair_name],
2131                    pair_name,
2132                    interaction_map_dir,
2133                    map_type,
2134                    cutoff,
2135                    self.molwise_residues,
2136                    self.map_slices[pair_name],
2137                    plotting_lib,
2138                    binarize_map,
2139                )
2140
2141        if "patches" in output_types:
2142            if not binarize_map:
2143                pairwise_maps = {
2144                    pair_name: get_binary_map(
2145                        q_map=pairwise_maps[pair_name].astype(self.f_dtype),
2146                        binarization_cutoff=cutoff,
2147                        map_type=map_type,
2148                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
2149                    )
2150                    for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys()
2151                }
2152
2153            for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
2154
2155                executor.submit(
2156                    Interaction.matrix_patches_worker,
2157                    pairwise_maps[pair_name].astype(self.i_dtype),
2158                    pair_name,
2159                    interaction_map_dir,
2160                )
2161
2162        executor.shutdown(wait=False)
2163        print(f"Saved {map_type} maps and plots to {interaction_map_dir}")
2164
2165    @staticmethod
2166    def matrix_patches_worker(
2167        cmap: npt.NDArray[np.integer],
2168        pair_name: str,
2169        interaction_map_dir: str,
2170    ) -> None:
2171        """ Extract interacting patches from the contact map and save them as csvs.
2172
2173        ## Arguments:
2174
2175        - **cmap (npt.NDArray[np.integer])**:<br />
2176            The binary contact map from which to extract patches.
2177
2178        - **pair_name (str)**:<br />
2179            The name of the molecule pair corresponding to the contact map (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2").
2180
2181        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
2182            The directory where the patch files will be saved.
2183        """
2184
2185        _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
2186        _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
2187        _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
2188        mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
2189        mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
2190
2191        assert all([range1 is not None, range2 is not None]), (
2192            f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {(_m1, _m2)}. "\
2193            "Expected format: MOL_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"
2194        )
2195
2196        # cheap trick to avoid df.groupby() error
2197        # `df.grouby()` will fail if row_obj and col_obj are the same
2198        if mol1 == mol2:
2199            mol1 += "-1"
2200            mol2 += "-2"
2201
2202        region_of_interest = {
2203            mol1: [
2204                get_res_range_from_key(range1)[0],
2205                get_res_range_from_key(range1)[1]
2206            ],
2207            mol2: [
2208                get_res_range_from_key(range2)[0],
2209                get_res_range_from_key(range2)[1]
2210            ]
2211        }
2212
2213        if len(np.unique(cmap)) == 1 and np.unique(cmap)[0] == 0:
2214            # print(f"No contacts found for {pair_name}, skipping patches.")
2215            return None
2216
2217        matrix_patches = MatrixPatches(
2218            matrix=cmap,
2219            row_obj=mol1,
2220            col_obj=mol2,
2221        )
2222
2223        patches_df = matrix_patches.get_patches_from_matrix()
2224
2225        ch1_p = [
2226            np.array(list(patch)) + region_of_interest[mol1][0]
2227            for patch in patches_df[mol1].tolist()
2228        ]
2229        ch2_p = [
2230            np.array(list(patch)) + region_of_interest[mol2][0]
2231            for patch in patches_df[mol2].tolist()
2232        ]
2233
2234        patches = {
2235            patch_idx: {
2236                mol1: ch1_patch,
2237                mol2: ch2_patch,
2238            } for patch_idx, (ch1_patch, ch2_patch) in enumerate(zip(ch1_p, ch2_p))
2239        }
2240
2241        if len(patches) > 0:
2242
2243            pair_name = (
2244                f"{mol1.replace('-1', '')}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
2245                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2246                f"{mol2.replace('-2', '')}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
2247            )
2248
2249            save_map(
2250                contact_map=cmap,
2251                avg_contact_probs_mat=None,
2252                patches=patches,
2253                chain1=mol1,
2254                chain2=mol2,
2255                p1_name=mol1,
2256                p2_name=mol2,
2257                p1_region=region_of_interest[mol1],
2258                p2_region=region_of_interest[mol2],
2259                out_file=Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"patches_{pair_name}.png",
2260                save_plot=False,
2261                verbose=False,
2262                # plot_type="static",
2263                # concat_residues=True,
2264                # contact_probability=False,
2265            )
2266
2267    @staticmethod
2268    def plot_map(
2269        q_map: npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating],
2270        pair_name: str,
2271        save_dir: str,
2272        map_type: str,
2273        cutoff: float,
2274        molwise_residues: dict,
2275        map_slice_dict: dict,
2276        plotting: str = "matplotlib",
2277        binarize_map: bool = True,
2278    ):
2279        """ Plot the contact or distance map.
2280
2281        ## Arguments:
2282
2283        - **q_map (npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating])**:<br />
2284            The distance or contact map to be plotted.
2285
2286        - **pair_name (str)**:<br />
2287            The name of the molecule pair corresponding to the map (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2").
2288
2289        - **save_dir (str)**:<br />
2290            The directory where the plot will be saved.
2291
2292        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
2293            A string indicating the type of map being plotted.
2294            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
2295
2296        - **cutoff (float)**:<br />
2297            The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be
2298            included in the plot title and colorbar label. See :func:`get_binary_map`
2299            for more details.
2300
2301        - **molwise_residues (dict)**:<br />
2302            A dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of residue numbers.
2303            Format:
2304            {
2305                "MOL1": [residue numbers],
2306                "MOL2": [residue numbers],
2307                ...
2308            }
2309
2310        - **plotting (str, optional):**:<br />
2311            The plotting backend to use. Can be either "matplotlib" or "plotly".
2312
2313        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
2314            Whether to binarize the map before plotting.
2315        """
2316
2317        _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
2318        mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
2319        mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
2320
2321        map_titles = {
2322            "dmap": {
2323                True: f"Binarized Average Distance Map (cutoff={cutoff} Å): {mol1}{PAIR_SEP}{mol2}",
2324                False: f"Average Distance Map (Å): {mol1}{PAIR_SEP}{mol2}",
2325            },
2326            "cmap": {
2327                True: f"Binarized Average Contact Map (cutoff={cutoff}) : {mol1}{PAIR_SEP}{mol2}",
2328                False: f'Average Contact Map (cutoff={cutoff}) : {mol1}{PAIR_SEP}{mol2}',
2329            },
2330        }
2331        map_labels = {
2332            "dmap": {
2333                True: 'Contact (1) / No Contact (0)',
2334                False: 'Average Distance (Å)',
2335            },
2336            "cmap": {
2337                True: 'Contact (1) / No Contact (0)',
2338                False: 'Fraction of Frames in Contact',
2339            }
2340        }
2341        max_vals = {
2342            "dmap": {
2343                True: 1,
2344                False: np.max(q_map),

2445    @staticmethod
2446    def extract_interface_residues_from_patches(
2447        interacting_patches_csvs: list[str],
2448    ):
2449        """ Extract interface residue information from interaction map patch CSV files.
2450
2451        ## Arguments:
2452
2453        - **interacting_patches_csvs (str)**:<br />
2454            A list of paths to CSV files containing the interacting patches
2455            extracted from the contact maps. Each CSV file should have columns
2456            corresponding to the molecule names (e.g. "MOL1", "MOL2")
2457
2458        ## Returns:
2459
2460        - **dict**:<br />
2461            A dictionary mapping interface names to sets of residue pairs.
2462            The keys are interface names in the format "Protein1_Protein2", and the
2463            values are sets of tuples, where each tuple contains the residue ranges
2464            for the interacting residues from the two proteins (e.g.,
2465            ("res1_start-res1_end", "res2_start-res2_end")).
2466        """
2467
2468        interface_dict = defaultdict(list)
2469
2470        for patches_csv_path in interacting_patches_csvs:
2471
2472            patches_df = pd.read_csv(patches_csv_path, header=0)
2473            prot1_n, prot2_n = list(patches_df.columns)
2474            if "_" in prot1_n:
2475                _prot1_n = prot1_n.split("_")[0]
2476            if "_" in prot2_n:
2477                _prot2_n = prot2_n.split("_")[0]
2478
2479            interface_name = f"{_prot1_n.split("-")[0]}_{_prot2_n.split("-")[0]}"
2480            interface_dict[interface_name] = set()
2481
2482            for _, row in patches_df.iterrows():
2483                interface_dict[interface_name].add((row[prot1_n], row[prot2_n]))
2484
2485        return interface_dict
2486

def read_molecules_from_file( input: str, key: str | None = None) -> Tuple[List[str], List[Dict[str, float]], List[str]]: 
48def read_molecules_from_file(
49    input: str,
50    key: str | None=None,
51) -> Tuple[List[str], List[Dict[str, float]], List[str]]:
52
53    if input.endswith('.json'):
54        data = read_json(input)
55
56    elif input.endswith('.yaml') or input.endswith('.yml'):
57        import yaml
58        with open(input, 'r') as f:
59            data = yaml.load(f, Loader=yaml.FullLoader)
60
61    else:
62        raise ValueError("Input file must be JSON or YAML format.")
63
64    if key is not None:
65        data = data[key]
66
67    molecules = [_pt["molecule"] for _pt in data]
68    extra_attrs = []
69    extra_keys = sorted(list(set(data[0].keys()) - {"molecule"}))
70    for k in extra_keys:
71        extra_attrs.append({_pt["molecule"]: _pt[k] for _pt in data})
72
73    for m in molecules:
74        match = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m)
75        if match is None or len(match.groups()) != 3:
76            raise ValueError(
77                f"Invalid molecule name format: {m}."\
78                f"Expected formats: {", ".join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
79            )
80
81    return molecules, extra_attrs, extra_keys
def read_molecule_pairs_from_file(input: str, key: str | None = None) -> List[tuple]: 
 83def read_molecule_pairs_from_file(input: str, key: str | None=None) ->List[tuple]:
 84    """ Extract molecule pairs from a json file.
 85
 86    A molcule refers to a specific copy of the modeled protein. e.g. DSC2a_0.
 87    The molecule pairs should be specified as follows:
 88
 89    [
 90        ["MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND", "MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"],
 91        ["MOL3_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND", "MOL4_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"],
 92        ...
 93    ]
 94
 95    ## Arguments:
 96
 97    - **input (str)**:<br />
 98        Path to the JSON file containing the molecule pairs.
 99
100    ## Returns:
101
102    - **list**:<br />
103        A list of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format
104        (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
105    """
106
107    if input.endswith('.json'):
108        data = read_json(input)
109        if key is not None:
110            data = data[key]
111    elif input.endswith('.yaml') or input.endswith('.yml'):
112        import yaml
113        with open(input, 'r') as f:
114            data = yaml.load(f, Loader=yaml.FullLoader)
115            if key is not None:
116                data = data[key]
117    else:
118        raise ValueError("Input file must be JSON or YAML format.")
119
120    mol_pairs = [(_pt["molecule1"], _pt["molecule2"]) for _pt in data]
121    extra_attrs = []
122    extra_keys = list(set(data[0].keys()) - {"molecule1", "molecule2"})
123    for k in extra_keys:
124        extra_attrs.append({
125            (_pt["molecule1"], _pt["molecule2"]): _pt[k] for _pt in data
126        })
127
128    for m1, m2 in mol_pairs:
129        match1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1)
130        match2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2)
131        if match1 is None or len(match1.groups()) != 3:
132            raise ValueError(
133                f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {m1}. "\
134                f"Expected format is one of: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
135            )
136
137        if match2 is None or len(match2.groups()) != 3:
138            raise ValueError(
139                f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {m2}. "\
140                f"Expected format is one of: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
141            )
142
143    return mol_pairs, extra_attrs, extra_keys

Extract molecule pairs from a json file.

A molcule refers to a specific copy of the modeled protein. e.g. DSC2a_0. The molecule pairs should be specified as follows:

[ ["MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND", "MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"], ["MOL3_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND", "MOL4_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"], ... ]

Arguments:

  • input (str):
    Path to the JSON file containing the molecule pairs.

Returns:

  • list:
    A list of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).

147    def __init__(
148        self,
149        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,

151    ):
152
153        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
154        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
155        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
156
157        if isinstance(input, str):
158            (
159                self.molecules,
160                self.extra_attrs,
161                self.extra_attrs_keys,
162            ) = read_molecules_from_file(input=input)

166        else:

168
169    def process_molecules(self, filter_by: list = []) -> List[str]:
170
171        self.enrich_molecules()
172        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
173            self.enrich_attributes()
174
175        if len(filter_by) > 0:
176            self.filter_molecules(
177                filter_by=filter_by,
178                filter_level="copy",
179            )
180
181        return self.molecules
182
183    def filter_molecules(self, filter_by: list, filter_level: str = "copy",) -> None:
184
185        assert filter_level in ["copy", "base"], "filter_level must be either 'copy' or 'base'"
186
187        _filter = {"copy": False, "base": True}
188
189        _filtered = [
190            XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m, _filter[filter_level]) for m in filter_by
191        ]
192
193        self.molecules = sorted(set([
194            m for m in self.molecules
195            if (
196                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m, _filter[filter_level]) in _filtered
197            )
198        ]))
199
200        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
201            self.extra_attrs = [
202                {m: attr[m] for m in self.molecules if m in attr}
203                for attr in self.extra_attrs
204            ]
205            self.extra_attrs = [
206                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
207                for attr in self.extra_attrs
208            ]
209
210    def enrich_molecules(self) -> List[str]:
211
212        enriched_molecules = []
213        for m in self.molecules:
214            _enriched = self.enrich_molecule(m, fix_range=True)
215            enriched_molecules.extend(_enriched)
216
217        self.molecules = sorted(set(enriched_molecules))
218
219    def enrich_attributes(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
220
221        enriched_attrs = []
222
223        for attr in self.extra_attrs:
224            enriched_attr = {
225                en_m: val for m, val in attr.items()
226                for en_m in self.enrich_molecule(m, fix_range=True)
227            }
228            enriched_attrs.append(enriched_attr)
229
230        # sorted by molecule name
231        self.extra_attrs = [
232            dict(sorted(enriched_attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
233            for enriched_attr in enriched_attrs
234        ]
235
236    def raise_invalid_range_error(self, mol, specified_range):
237
238        valid_range = set(self.molwise_residues[mol])
239        specified_range_set = set(get_res_range_from_key(specified_range))
240
241        if not specified_range_set.issubset(valid_range):
242            raise ValueError(
243                f"{mol}:{specified_range} is invalid. "\
244                f"Valid residues - {mol}:{get_key_from_res_range(valid_range)}"
245            )
246
247    @property
248    def _enricher(self):
249        return {
250            True: lambda m, sel: f"{m}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{sel}",
251            False: lambda m, sel: (
252                f"{m}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}"
253                f"{get_key_from_res_range(self.molwise_residues[m])}"
254            ),
255        }
256
257    @property
258    def _range_checker(self):
259        return {
260            True: self.raise_invalid_range_error,
261            False: lambda mol, specified_range: None,
262        }
263
264    def enrich_molecule(self, m, fix_range: bool = False) -> List[str]:
265
266        enriched_molecules = []
267
268        try:
269            base, cp_idx, sel = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m).groups()
270
271        except Exception as e:
272            raise ValueError(
273                f"Invalid format for molecule: {m}. "\
274                f"Expected formats: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
275            ) from e
276
277        copies_m = self.xyzr_parser.get_verify_copies(
278            mol_basename=base,
279            copy_idx=cp_idx,
280        )
281
282        for cpy in copies_m:
283
284            condition = sel is not None and sel != ""
285            if fix_range:
286                valid_range = set(self.molwise_residues[cpy])
287                specified_range_set = set(get_res_range_from_key(sel))
288                common_range = valid_range.intersection(specified_range_set)
289                common_range_key = get_key_from_res_range(common_range)
290            else:
291                self._range_checker[condition](cpy, sel)
292                common_range_key = sel
293            enriched_molecules.append(self._enricher[condition](cpy, common_range_key))
294
295        return enriched_molecules

169    def process_molecules(self, filter_by: list = []) -> List[str]:

171        self.enrich_molecules()
172        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
173            self.enrich_attributes()
174
175        if len(filter_by) > 0:
176            self.filter_molecules(
177                filter_by=filter_by,
178                filter_level="copy",
179            )
180
181        return self.molecules
def filter_molecules(self, filter_by: list, filter_level: str = 'copy') -> None: 
183    def filter_molecules(self, filter_by: list, filter_level: str = "copy",) -> None:
184
185        assert filter_level in ["copy", "base"], "filter_level must be either 'copy' or 'base'"
186
187        _filter = {"copy": False, "base": True}
188
189        _filtered = [

191        ]
192
193        self.molecules = sorted(set([
194            m for m in self.molecules

197            )
198        ]))
199
200        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
201            self.extra_attrs = [
202                {m: attr[m] for m in self.molecules if m in attr}
203                for attr in self.extra_attrs
204            ]
205            self.extra_attrs = [
206                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
207                for attr in self.extra_attrs
208            ]
def enrich_molecules(self) -> List[str]:

212        enriched_molecules = []

227            }
228            enriched_attrs.append(enriched_attr)

def raise_invalid_range_error(self, mol, specified_range): 
236    def raise_invalid_range_error(self, mol, specified_range):
237
238        valid_range = set(self.molwise_residues[mol])
239        specified_range_set = set(get_res_range_from_key(specified_range))
240
241        if not specified_range_set.issubset(valid_range):
242            raise ValueError(
243                f"{mol}:{specified_range} is invalid. "\
244                f"Valid residues - {mol}:{get_key_from_res_range(valid_range)}"
245            )
def enrich_molecule(self, m, fix_range: bool = False) -> List[str]: 
264    def enrich_molecule(self, m, fix_range: bool = False) -> List[str]:
265
266        enriched_molecules = []
267
268        try:
269            base, cp_idx, sel = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m).groups()
270
271        except Exception as e:
272            raise ValueError(
273                f"Invalid format for molecule: {m}. "\
274                f"Expected formats: {', '.join(EXPECTED_MOLNAME_FORMATS)}"
275            ) from e
276
277        copies_m = self.xyzr_parser.get_verify_copies(
278            mol_basename=base,
279            copy_idx=cp_idx,
280        )
281
282        for cpy in copies_m:
283
284            condition = sel is not None and sel != ""
285            if fix_range:
286                valid_range = set(self.molwise_residues[cpy])
287                specified_range_set = set(get_res_range_from_key(sel))
288                common_range = valid_range.intersection(specified_range_set)
289                common_range_key = get_key_from_res_range(common_range)
290            else:
291                self._range_checker[condition](cpy, sel)
292                common_range_key = sel
293            enriched_molecules.append(self._enricher[condition](cpy, common_range_key))
294
295        return enriched_molecules
class MoleculePairs: 
297class MoleculePairs:
298    """ Class to handle molecule pair data during interaction map generation."""
299
300    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
301    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
302
303    molwise_residues: Dict[str, list]
304    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to sets of residue numbers. Format: {
305        "MOL1_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
306        "MOL2_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
307        ...
308    } """
309
310    self_interaction: str
311    """ String indicating how to handle self-interactions. Should be one of:
312    - "allow_all": allow interactions between all molecule pairs, including
313                   self-pairs and copy pairs.
314    - "allow_none": disallow interactions between any molecule pairs of the same
315                    molecule, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
316    - "allow_copies": allow interactions between different copies of the same
317                      molecule, but disallow self-pairs. (default)
318    """
319
320    unique_mols: set
321    """ Set of unique molecule names (without copy index) present in the model. """
322
323    mol_pairs: list
324    """ List of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format
325    (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
326    This list is processed and enriched based on the specified molecule pairs"""
327
328    def __init__(
329        self,
330        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
331        input: str | None = None,
332        self_interaction: str = "allow_copies",
333    ):
334
335        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
336        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
337        self.self_interaction = self_interaction
338        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
339        self.molecule_handler = Molecules(xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser)
340
341        if isinstance(input, str):
342            (
343                self.mol_pairs,
344                self.extra_attrs,
345                self.extra_attrs_keys,
346            ) = read_molecule_pairs_from_file(input=input)
347        else:
348            self.mol_pairs = list(
349                combinations_with_replacement(sorted(self.unique_mols), 2)
350            )
351
352    @staticmethod
353    def get_grouped_mol_pairs(mol_pairs: list) -> Dict[str, set]:
354        """ Group molecule pairs by their base molecule names and residuerange,
355        ignoring copy indices.
356
357        ## Arguments:
358
359        - **mol_pairs (list)**:<br />
360            A list of tuples containing the molecule pairs in the format
361            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
362
363        ## Returns:
364
365        - **dict**:<br />
366            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (without copy indices) to
367            sets of molecule pairs (with copy indices) that belong to that pair
368            name. The keys of the dictionary are in the format:
369            "MOL1:RESSTART-RESEND:MOL2:RESSTART-RESEND" and the values are sets
370            of tuples in the format:
371            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
372        """
373
374        grouped_mol_pairs = defaultdict(set)
375
376        for m1, m2 in mol_pairs:
377            base1, _, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1).groups()
378            base2, _, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2).groups()
379            pair_name = (
380                f"{base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
381                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
382                f"{base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
383            )
384            grouped_mol_pairs[pair_name].add((m1, m2))
385
386        return grouped_mol_pairs
387
388    def process_molecule_pairs(self, filter_by: list = []) -> List[tuple]:
389        """ Process and enrich molecule pairs.
390
391        - Add copy indices and residue ranges.
392        - Filter by specified molecule pairs if filter_by is not empty.
393
394        ## Arguments:
395
396        - **filter_by (list, optional):**:<br />
397            A list of tuples specifying molecule pairs to filter by. Each tuple
398            should be in the format:
399            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND) where,
400            COPYIDX and RESSTART-RESEND are be optional.
401
402        ## Returns:
403
404        - **list**:<br />
405            A list of tuples containing the processed molecule pairs in the format
406            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND).
407        """
408
409        self._enrich_mol_pairs()
410        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
411            self._enrich_attributes()
412
413        self._filter_self_pairs()
414
415        if len(filter_by) > 0:
416            self._filter_mol_pairs(
417                filter_by=filter_by,
418                filter_level="copy",
419            )
420
421        return self.mol_pairs
422
423    def _enrich_mol_pairs(self) -> None:
424        """ Enrich molecule pairs
425
426        - Add copy indices and residue ranges to the molecule pairs.
427        """
428
429        enriched_mol_pairs = []
430
431        for m1, m2 in self.mol_pairs:
432
433            enriched_m1 = self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m1)
434            enriched_m2 = self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m2)
435
436            for cpy1, cpy2 in product(enriched_m1, enriched_m2):
437                enriched_mol_pairs.append((cpy1, cpy2))
438
439        self.mol_pairs = list(set(enriched_mol_pairs))
440
441    def _enrich_attributes(self) -> None:
442
443        enriched_attrs = []
444
445        for attr in self.extra_attrs:
446            enriched_attr = {
447                (en_m1, en_m2): val
448                for (m1, m2), val in attr.items()
449                for en_m1 in self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m1)
450                for en_m2 in self.molecule_handler.enrich_molecule(m2)
451            }
452            enriched_attrs.append(enriched_attr)
453
454        # sorted by molecule pair
455        self.extra_attrs = [
456            dict(sorted(enriched_attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
457            for enriched_attr in enriched_attrs
458        ]
459
460    def _filter_mol_pairs(
461        self,
462        filter_by: List[tuple],
463        filter_level: str = "copy",
464    ) -> None:
465        """ Filter molecule pairs by specified molecule pairs.
466
467        ## Arguments:
468
469        - **filter_by (List[tuple])**:<br />
470            A list of tuples specifying molecule pairs to filter by. Each tuple
471            should be in the format:
472            (MOL1_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND, MOL2_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND) where,
473            COPYIDX and RESSTART-RESEND are be optional.
474
475        - **filter_level (str, optional):**:<br />
476            The level at which to apply the filter. Should be either "copy" or "base".
477            - "copy": filter by the full molecule pair names including copy indices
478                      and residue ranges. (default)
479            - "base": filter by the base molecule names only, ignoring copy indices
480                      and residue ranges.
481        """
482
483        assert filter_level in ["copy", "base"], "filter_level must be either 'copy' or 'base'"
484
485        _filter = {"copy": False, "base": True}
486
487        def get_mol_pair_names(pair):
488            m1, m2 = pair
489            return (
490                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m1, _filter[filter_level]),
491                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m2, _filter[filter_level])
492            )
493
494        _filtered_mol_pairs = [
495            (
496                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m1, _filter[filter_level]),
497                XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m2, _filter[filter_level])
498            )
499            for m1, m2 in filter_by
500        ]
501
502        self.mol_pairs = list(set([
503            pair for pair in self.mol_pairs
504            if (
505                get_mol_pair_names(pair) in _filtered_mol_pairs or
506                tuple(reversed(get_mol_pair_names(pair))) in _filtered_mol_pairs
507            )
508        ]))
509
510        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
511            self.extra_attrs = [
512                {
513                    pair: attr[pair] for pair in self.mol_pairs if pair in attr
514                }
515                for attr in self.extra_attrs
516            ]
517            self.extra_attrs = [
518                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
519                for attr in self.extra_attrs
520            ]
521
522    def _filter_self_pairs(self) -> None:
523        """ Remove self-interactions based on self.self_interaction attribute."""
524
525        pairs_to_remove = set()
526
527        _do_dict = {
528            "allow_all": lambda b1, c1, b2, c2: False,
529            "allow_none": lambda b1, c1, b2, c2: b1 == b2,
530            "allow_copies": lambda b1, c1, b2, c2: (b1 == b2) and (c1 == c2),
531        }
532
533        for m1, m2 in self.mol_pairs:
534
535            base1, cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1).groups()
536            base2, cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2).groups()
537            assert (
538                all([base1 is not None, base2 is not None]) and
539                all([cp_idx1 is not None, cp_idx2 is not None])
540            ), (
541                f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {(m1, m2)}. "\
542                "Expected format: MOL_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"
543            )
544
545            if _do_dict[self.self_interaction](base1, cp_idx1, base2, cp_idx2):
546                pairs_to_remove.add((m1, m2))
547
548        self.mol_pairs = [
549            pair for pair in self.mol_pairs
550            if pair not in pairs_to_remove
551        ]
552
553        if hasattr(self, "extra_attrs"):
554            self.extra_attrs = [
555                {
556                    pair: attr[pair] for pair in self.mol_pairs if pair in attr
557                }
558                for attr in self.extra_attrs
559            ]
560            self.extra_attrs = [
561                dict(sorted(attr.items(), key=lambda x: x[0]))
562                for attr in self.extra_attrs
563            ]

def explode_map( q_map: numpy.ndarray, mol: str, molwise_xyzr_keys: Dict[str, list], by: str = 'row') -> numpy.ndarray: 
565def explode_map(
566    q_map: np.ndarray,
567    mol: str,
568    molwise_xyzr_keys: Dict[str, list],
569    by: str = "row",
570) -> np.ndarray:
571    """ Expand a bead-level distance/contact map to residue-level map along
572    the specified axis.
573
574    ## Arguments:
575
576    - **q_map (np.ndarray)**:<br />
577        The distance/contact map to be expanded.
578
579    - **mol (str)**:<br />
580        The molecule name for which the map is being expanded (e.g. "MOL_COPYIDX").
581
582    - **by (str, optional):**:<br />
583        The axis along which to expand the map. Should be either "row" or "col".
584
585    ## Returns:
586
587    - **np.ndarray**:<br />
588        The expanded distance/contact map.
589    """
590
591    assert q_map.ndim == 2, "q_map must be a 2D array."
592
593    repeat_ = {
594        "row": lambda q, i: q[i, :],
595        "col": lambda q, i: q[:, i],
596    }
597
598    axis_ = {"row": 0, "col": 1}
599
600    special_keys = [
601        (key.rsplit("_", 1)[1], idx)
602        for idx, key in enumerate(molwise_xyzr_keys[mol])
603        if "-" in key
604    ]
605    dup_attrs = []
606
607    for key, attr_idx in special_keys:
608        num_repeats = len(get_res_range_from_key(key))
609        to_add = np.tile(repeat_[by](q_map, attr_idx), (num_repeats - 1, 1))
610        dup_attrs.append((to_add, attr_idx))
611
612    for to_add, attr_idx in reversed(dup_attrs):
613        q_map = np.insert(q_map, attr_idx + 1, to_add, axis=axis_[by])
614
615    return q_map

def expand_map_to_residue_level( q_map: numpy.ndarray, molwise_xyzr_keys: dict, pair_name: str) -> numpy.ndarray: 
617def expand_map_to_residue_level(
618    q_map: np.ndarray,
619    molwise_xyzr_keys: dict,
620    pair_name: str,
621) -> np.ndarray:
622    """ Expand a bead-level distance/contact map to residue-level map.
623
624    ## Arguments:
625
626    - **q_map (np.ndarray)**:<br />
627        Original distance/contact map.
628
629    - **pair_name (str)**:<br />
630        The name of the molecule pair. (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
631
632    ## Returns:
633
634    - **np.ndarray**:<br />
635        Expanded distance/contact map.
636    """
637
638    _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
639    base1, cp_idx1, _ = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
640    base2, cp_idx2, _ = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
641    mol1 = f"{base1}{MOL_COPY_SEP}{cp_idx1}"
642    mol2 = f"{base2}{MOL_COPY_SEP}{cp_idx2}"
643
644    # expand the maps to include all residues in the selection
645    q_map = explode_map(q_map, mol1, molwise_xyzr_keys, by="row")
646    q_map = explode_map(q_map, mol2, molwise_xyzr_keys, by="col")
647
648    return q_map

  • np.ndarray:
    Expanded distance/contact map.
def get_binary_map( q_map: numpy.ndarray[tuple[typing.Any, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.integer]] | numpy.ndarray[tuple[typing.Any, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.floating]], binarization_cutoff: float, map_type: str = 'dmap', i_dtype: numpy.dtype = <class 'numpy.int32'>) -> numpy.ndarray[tuple[typing.Any, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.integer]] | numpy.ndarray[tuple[typing.Any, ...], numpy.dtype[numpy.floating]]: 
650def get_binary_map(
651    q_map: npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating],
652    binarization_cutoff: float,
653    map_type: str = "dmap",
654    i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
655) -> npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating]:
656    """ Convert the distance or contact map to binary map based on cutoff.
657
658    ## Arguments:
659
660    - **q_map (npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating])**:<br />
661        The distance or contact map to be binarized.
662
663    - **binarization_cutoff (float)**:<br />
664        The cutoff value used for binarization.
665        - For distance maps, this is the maximum distance for a pair to be
666        considered in contact.
667        - For contact maps, this is the minimum fraction of frames which should
668        have the pair in contact for it to be considered a contact.
669
670    - **map_type (str, optional):**:<br />
671        The type of map being binarized.
672        Either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
673
674    - **i_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
675        The integer data type to be used for the binary map.
676
677    ## Returns:
678
679    - **npt.NDArray[np.integer] | npt.NDArray[np.floating]**:<br />
680        The binary map.
681    """
682
683    if map_type == "dmap":
684        q_map[q_map < binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(1)
685        q_map[q_map >= binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(0)
686
687    elif map_type == "cmap":
688        q_map[q_map >= binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(1)
689        q_map[q_map < binarization_cutoff] = i_dtype(0)
690
691    q_map = q_map.astype(i_dtype)
692
693    return q_map

class PairwiseMaps: 
 727class PairwiseMaps:
 728    """ Class to handle pairwise distance and contact maps for given molecule pairs."""
 729
 730    mol_pairs: list
 731    """ List of enriched molecule pairs. See `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
 732
 733    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
 734    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
 735
 736    xyzr_mat: np.ndarray
 737    """ The raw XYZR data as a numpy array of shape (num_beads, num_frames, 4). """
 738
 739    xyzr_keys: list
 740    """ List of bead keys in the format "MOL_COPYIDX_RESNUM" or "MOL_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND",
 741    corresponding to the rows in xyzr_mat. """
 742
 743    molwise_residues: dict
 744    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to sets of residue numbers. Format: {
 745        "MOL1_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
 746        "MOL2_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...],
 747        ...
 748    } """
 749
 750    molwise_xyzr_keys: dict
 751    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of bead keys. Format: {
 752        "MOL1_COPYIDX": ["MOL1_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...],
 753        "MOL2_COPYIDX": ["MOL2_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...],
 754        ...
 755    } """
 756
 757    self_interaction: str
 758    """ String indicating how to handle self-interactions. Should be one of:
 759    - "allow_all": allow interactions between all molecule pairs, including
 760                   self-pairs and copy pairs.
 761    - "allow_none": disallow interactions between any molecule pairs of the same
 762                    molecule, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
 763    - "allow_copies": allow interactions between different copies of the same
 764                      molecule, but disallow self-pairs. (default)
 765    """
 766
 767    unique_mols: set
 768    """ Set of unique molecule names (without copy index) present in the model. """
 769
 770    f_dtype: np.dtype
 771    """ The floating point data type to use for the distance and contact maps. """
 772
 773    i_dtype: np.dtype
 774    """ The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps. """
 775
 776    contact_cutoff: float
 777    """ The cutoff distance used for binarization of the distance maps, which will be
 778    passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
 779    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
 780    """
 781
 782    fraction_cutoff: float
 783    """ The cutoff fraction used for binarization of the contact maps, which will
 784    be passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
 785    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
 786    """
 787
 788    def __init__(
 789        self,
 790        mol_pairs: list,
 791        xyzr_parser: XYZRParser,
 792        contact_cutoff: float,
 793        fraction_cutoff: float,
 794        self_interaction: bool = False,
 795        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
 796        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
 797    ):
 798
 799        self.mol_pairs = mol_pairs
 800        self.xyzr_parser = xyzr_parser
 801        self.xyzr_mat = xyzr_parser.xyzr_mat
 802        self.xyzr_keys = xyzr_parser.xyzr_keys
 803        self.num_frames = xyzr_parser.xyzr_mat.shape[1]
 804        self.molwise_residues = xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
 805        self.molwise_xyzr_keys = xyzr_parser.molwise_xyzr_keys
 806        self.self_interaction = self_interaction
 807        self.unique_mols = xyzr_parser.unique_mols
 808        self.f_dtype = f_dtype
 809        self.i_dtype = i_dtype
 810        self.contact_cutoff = contact_cutoff
 811        self.fraction_cutoff = fraction_cutoff
 812
 813    def process_pairwise_maps(
 814        self,
 815        pairwise_maps: dict,
 816        map_type: str,
 817        merge_operation: str = "average",
 818        merge_copies: bool = False,
 819        binarize_map: bool = False,
 820    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
 821        """ Process pairwise distance or contact maps by expanding to residue-level,
 822        merging across copies if specified, and binarizing if specified.
 823
 824        ## Arguments:
 825
 826        - **pairwise_maps (dict)**:<br />
 827            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
 828            to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 829
 830        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
 831            A string indicating the type of maps being processed.
 832            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
 833
 834        - **merge_copies (bool, optional):**:<br />
 835            Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the
 836            maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps
 837            will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the `merge_maps_by_copies`
 838            function. If False, the maps will be processed separately for each copy pair.
 839
 840        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
 841            Whether to binarize the maps based on the cutoff. If True, the maps will be
 842            converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a contact is
 843            defined as present if it is present in any of the copy pairs (if merge_copies
 844            is True) or based on the cutoff for each individual map (if merge_copies is False).
 845            If False, the maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values.
 846
 847        ## Returns:
 848
 849        - **dict**:<br />
 850            A dictionary of processed interaction maps per molecule pair.
 851        """
 852
 853        assert map_type in ["dmap", "cmap"], "map_type must be either 'dmap' or 'cmap'"
 854
 855        ############################################################################
 856        # Expand the maps to residue-level for plotting and patch extraction.
 857        ############################################################################
 858        for pair_name, pairwise_map in pairwise_maps.items():
 859
 860            pairwise_maps[pair_name] = expand_map_to_residue_level(
 861                q_map=pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype),
 862                molwise_xyzr_keys=self.molwise_xyzr_keys,
 863                pair_name=pair_name
 864            )
 865
 866        ############################################################################
 867        # Merge maps across copies if specified, and binarize if specified.
 868        ############################################################################
 869        if merge_copies:
 870
 871            pairwise_maps = self.merge_maps_by_copies(
 872                pairwise_maps=pairwise_maps,
 873                map_type=map_type,
 874                operation="or" if binarize_map else merge_operation,
 875                binarize_map=binarize_map,
 876            )
 877
 878        else:
 879
 880            for pair_name, pairwise_map in pairwise_maps.items():
 881
 882                if binarize_map:
 883                    pairwise_maps[pair_name] = get_binary_map(
 884                        q_map=pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype),
 885                        binarization_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff if map_type=="dmap" else self.fraction_cutoff,
 886                        map_type=map_type,
 887                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype
 888                    )
 889
 890                else:
 891                    pairwise_maps[pair_name] = pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype)
 892
 893        return pairwise_maps
 894
 895    def prepare_xyzr_batches(
 896        self,
 897        frame_batches: List[np.ndarray],
 898        res_range: Optional[str],
 899        mol_name: str
 900    ) -> Tuple[List[int], List[np.ndarray]]:
 901        """ Prepare batches of XYZR data for the specified molecule and residue range.
 902
 903        ## Arguments:
 904
 905        - **frame_batches (List[np.ndarray])**:<br />
 906            A list of numpy arrays, where each array contains the frame indices
 907            for a batch.
 908
 909        - **res_range (Optional[str])**:<br />
 910            A string specifying the residue range to select for the molecule.
 911            Should be in the format "RESSTART-RESEND". If None, all residues for
 912            the molecule will be selected.
 913
 914        - **mol_name (str)**:<br />
 915            The name of the molecule for which to prepare the XYZR batches. Should
 916            be in the format "MOL_COPYIDX".
 917
 918        ## Returns:
 919
 920        - **Tuple[List[int], List[np.ndarray]]**:<br />
 921            A tuple containing:
 922            - A list of indices corresponding to the selected residues for the
 923              molecule.
 924            - A list of numpy arrays, where each array contains the XYZR data
 925              for the selected residues and frames in the corresponding batch.
 926        """
 927
 928        res_range = (
 929            get_res_range_from_key(res_range)
 930            if res_range is not None else self.molwise_residues[mol_name]
 931        )
 932
 933        idx = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol_name, res_range, self.xyzr_keys)
 934        xyzr = self.xyzr_mat[idx, :, :].astype(self.f_dtype)
 935        xyzr_batches = [
 936            xyzr[:, f_batch, :].astype(self.f_dtype)
 937            for f_batch in frame_batches
 938        ]
 939
 940        del xyzr
 941
 942        return idx, xyzr_batches
 943
 944    def merge_maps_by_copies(
 945        self,
 946        pairwise_maps: dict,
 947        map_type: str,
 948        operation: str = "average",
 949        binarize_map:bool = False,
 950    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
 951        """ Merge contact or distance maps across copy pairs.
 952
 953        > [!NOTE]
 954        > if the binarize_map flag is set to True,
 955        > the merged map is a binary map where a contact is defined as present if
 956        > it is present in any of the copy pairs.
 957        >
 958        > if the binarize_map flag is set to False,
 959        > the merged map is - average of the distance/contact maps across copy pairs.
 960
 961        ## Arguments:
 962
 963        - **pairwise_maps (dict)**:<br />
 964            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
 965            to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 966
 967        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
 968            A string indicating the type of maps being merged.
 969            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
 970
 971        - **operation (str, optional):**:<br />
 972            The operation to use when merging the maps across copy pairs. Should be
 973            either "average" to take the average of the maps across copy pairs or "or"
 974            to take the logical OR of the maps across copy pairs when binarizing.
 975            (default: "average")
 976
 977        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
 978            Whether to binarize the merged maps based on the cutoff.
 979            - If True, the merged maps will be converted to binary maps using the
 980              `get_binary_map` function, where a contact is defined as present
 981               if it is present in any of the copy pairs.
 982            - If False, the merged maps will not be binarized and will retain
 983              their original values (e.g. average distances or contact frequencies).
 984              (default: False)
 985
 986        ## Returns:
 987
 988        - **dict**:<br />
 989            A dictionary mapping merged molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") to
 990            their corresponding merged distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 991        """
 992
 993        merged_pairwise_maps = defaultdict(list)
 994
 995        def raise_invalid_operation_error(operation):
 996            raise ValueError(f"Invalid operation: {operation}.")
 997
 998        func_ = {
 999            ("average", False): lambda v: np.mean(v, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1000            ("or", True): lambda v: np.logical_or.reduce(v, axis=0).astype(self.i_dtype),
1001            ("min", False): lambda v: np.min(np.stack(v, axis=0), axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1002            ("max", False): lambda v: np.max(np.stack(v, axis=0), axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1003        }.get(
1004            (operation, binarize_map),
1005            lambda v: raise_invalid_operation_error(operation)
1006        )
1007
1008        for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
1009
1010            _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
1011            base1, _, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1012            base2, _, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1013
1014            merged_pair_name = (
1015                f"{base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
1016                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
1017                f"{base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
1018            )
1019
1020            _map = pairwise_maps[pair_name].copy()
1021
1022            if binarize_map is True:
1023                _map = get_binary_map(
1024                    q_map=_map,
1025                    binarization_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff if map_type=="dmap" else self.fraction_cutoff,
1026                    map_type=map_type,
1027                    i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1028                )
1029
1030            merged_pairwise_maps[merged_pair_name].append(_map)
1031
1032        merged_pairwise_maps = {
1033            k: func_(v)
1034            for k, v in merged_pairwise_maps.items()
1035        }
1036
1037        return merged_pairwise_maps
1038
1039    def fetch_pairwise_distances(
1040        self,
1041        output_dir: str,
1042        nproc: int,
1043        operation: str="min",
1044        subtract_radii: bool=True,
1045        overwrite: bool=False,
1046    ) -> dict:
1047        """ Fetch pairwise distance maps from XYZR data.
1048
1049        ## Arguments:
1050
1051        - **xyzr_mat (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1052            Array of shape (num_beads, num_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for all
1053            beads across all frames.
1054
1055        - **xyzr_keys (list)**:<br />
1056            List of strings representing the keys for each bead in the XYZR data.
1057            Each key should be formatted as "MoleculeName_CopyIndex_ResidueRangeStart-ResidueRangeEnd".
1058
1059        - **mol_pairs (list)**:<br />
1060            List of tuples, where each tuple contains two strings representing the
1061            names of the molecules in a binding pair, including copy indices and residue range information.
1062                For example:
1063            ```
1064            [
1065                ("ProteinA_copy1_10-50", "ProteinB_copy1_20-60"),
1066                ("ProteinA_copy2_10-50", "ProteinB_copy2_20-60"),
1067                ("ProteinC_copy1_5-30", "ProteinD_copy1_15-45"),
1068                ("ProteinC_copy2_5-30", "ProteinD_copy2_15-45")
1069            ]
1070            ```
1071
1072        - **output_dir (str)**:<br />
1073            Directory to save output distance map files. Each pairwise distance map will
1074            be saved as a text file named "Molecule1_Molecule2_dmap.txt" in this directory.
1075
1076        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1077            Number of processes to use for parallel distance map calculations.
1078
1079        - **f_dtype (np.dtype)**:<br />
1080            Float dtype for distance calculations.
1081
1082        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1083            Whether to overwrite existing distance map files. If False and a distance
1084            map file already exists for a given pair, the function will load the
1085            distance map from the file instead of recalculating it. Defaults to False.
1086
1087        ## Returns:
1088
1089        - **dict**:<br />
1090            Dictionary where keys are pair names formatted as "Molecule1_Molecule2" and
1091            values are arrays of shape (num_frames,) containing the minimum distance
1092            across all bead pairs for each frame.
1093        """
1094
1095        funcs = {
1096            "min": np.min,
1097            "average": np.average,
1098        }
1099
1100        pairwise_dmaps = {}
1101
1102        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), nproc)
1103
1104        for _m1, _m2 in tqdm.tqdm(self.mol_pairs):
1105
1106            _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1107            _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1108
1109            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
1110            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
1111            pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}" # this should include copy idx
1112
1113            dmap_txt = Path(output_dir) / f"{pair_name}_dmap.txt"
1114
1115            if os.path.exists(dmap_txt) and overwrite is False:
1116                pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(
1117                    dmap_txt,
1118                    dtype=self.f_dtype,
1119                )
1120                continue
1121
1122            _idx1, xyzr1_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1123                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1124                res_range=range1,
1125                mol_name=mol1,
1126            )
1127
1128            _idx2, xyzr2_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1129                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1130                res_range=range2,
1131                mol_name=mol2,
1132            )
1133
1134            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1135                futures = [
1136                    executor.submit(
1137                        PairwiseMaps.get_pairwise_distances,
1138                        xyzr1_b,
1139                        xyzr2_b,
1140                        self.f_dtype,
1141                        subtract_radii
1142                    )
1143                    for xyzr1_b, xyzr2_b in zip(xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches)
1144                ]
1145                results = []
1146                for future in tqdm.tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures)):
1147                    results.append(future.result())
1148
1149            del xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches
1150
1151            dmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros(self.num_frames, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1152
1153            n_frames = 0
1154            for i, flat_dmap_ in enumerate(results):
1155                # from each flattened dmap of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, batch_frames),
1156                # we take the minimum distance across all bead pairs for each frame,
1157                # resulting in an array of shape (batch_frames,)
1158                frame_slice = slice(n_frames, n_frames + flat_dmap_.shape[1])
1159                # dmap_m1_m2[frame_slice] = np.min(flat_dmap_, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype)
1160                dmap_m1_m2[frame_slice] = funcs[operation](flat_dmap_, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype)
1161                n_frames += flat_dmap_.shape[1]
1162
1163            del results
1164
1165            pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = dmap_m1_m2.astype(self.f_dtype)
1166
1167            if not os.path.exists(dmap_txt) or overwrite:
1168                np.savetxt(dmap_txt, dmap_m1_m2, fmt="%.6f")
1169
1170        return pairwise_dmaps
1171
1172    def fetch_pairwise_maps(
1173        self,
1174        interaction_map_dir: str,
1175        nproc: int,
1176        overwrite: bool = False,
1177    ) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
1178        """ Fetch pairwise distance and contact maps for specified molecule pairs.
1179
1180        > [!NOTE]
1181        > The selection defined in `mol_pairs` matters here.
1182        > The maps will only be computed for the selected residue ranges.
1183
1184        ## Arguments:
1185
1186        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
1187            The directory where interaction maps are saved.
1188
1189        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1190            The number of processes to use for parallel computation.
1191
1192        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1193            Whether to overwrite existing interaction map files. If False, function
1194            will load existing maps from disk if they are available, and skip
1195            recomputation. Note that the plots are always overwritten to reflect the
1196            current binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if
1197            the files already exist.
1198
1199        ## Returns:
1200
1201        - **tuple**:<br />
1202            A tuple containing two dictionaries:
1203            - pairwise_dmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2")
1204            to their corresponding average distance maps (numpy arrays).
1205            - pairwise_cmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their
1206            corresponding average contact maps (numpy arrays).
1207        """
1208
1209        pairwise_dmaps = {}
1210        pairwise_cmaps = {}
1211
1212        # num_frames = self.xyzr_mat.shape[1]
1213        num_beads = self.xyzr_mat.shape[0]
1214        assert self.xyzr_mat.shape[2] == 4, "Expected last dimension of xyzr_mat to be 4 (XYZR)."
1215        assert num_beads == len(self.xyzr_keys), "Number of beads in xyzr_mat does not match length of bead keys."
1216
1217        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), nproc)
1218
1219        for _m1, _m2 in tqdm.tqdm(self.mol_pairs):
1220
1221            pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}"
1222
1223            dmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_dmap.txt"
1224            cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_cmap.txt"
1225
1226            _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1227            _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1228
1229            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
1230            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
1231
1232            if (
1233                dmap_file.exists() and cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False
1234            ):
1235
1236                pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file)
1237                pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(dmap_file)
1238                continue
1239
1240            idx1, xyzr1_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1241                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1242                res_range=range1,
1243                mol_name=mol1,
1244            )
1245
1246            idx2, xyzr2_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1247                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1248                res_range=range2,
1249                mol_name=mol2,
1250            )
1251
1252            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1253                futures = [
1254                    executor.submit(
1255                        PairwiseMaps.get_pairwise_maps,
1256                        xyzr1_b,
1257                        xyzr2_b,
1258                        self.contact_cutoff,
1259                        self.f_dtype,
1260                        self.i_dtype
1261                    )
1262                    for xyzr1_b, xyzr2_b in zip(xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches)
1263                ]
1264                results = []
1265                for future in tqdm.tqdm(
1266                    as_completed(futures), total=len(futures)
1267                ):
1268                    results.append(future.result())
1269
1270            del xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches
1271
1272            dmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros((len(idx1), len(idx2)), dtype=self.f_dtype)
1273            cmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros((len(idx1), len(idx2)), dtype=self.i_dtype)
1274
1275            for i, (dmap_, cmap_) in enumerate(results):
1276                np.add(dmap_m1_m2, dmap_, out=dmap_m1_m2, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1277                np.add(cmap_m1_m2, cmap_, out=cmap_m1_m2, dtype=self.i_dtype)
1278
1279            del results
1280
1281            pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = (
1282                dmap_m1_m2.astype(self.f_dtype) / self.f_dtype(self.num_frames)
1283            )
1284            pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = (
1285                cmap_m1_m2.astype(self.i_dtype) / self.f_dtype(self.num_frames)
1286            )
1287
1288            save_map_txt(
1289                q_map=pairwise_dmaps[pair_name],
1290                save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1291                map_name=f"{pair_name}_dmap",
1292                overwrite=overwrite,
1293            )
1294
1295            save_map_txt(
1296                q_map=pairwise_cmaps[pair_name],
1297                save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1298                map_name=f"{pair_name}_cmap",
1299                overwrite=overwrite,
1300            )
1301
1302        del self.xyzr_mat
1303
1304        return pairwise_dmaps, pairwise_cmaps
1305
1306    @staticmethod
1307    def get_pairwise_distances(
1308        xyzr1: np.ndarray,
1309        xyzr2: np.ndarray,
1310        f_dtype: np.dtype=np.float64,
1311        subtract_radii: bool=True,
1312    ):
1313        """ Given two arrays of XYZR, return all pairwise distances.
1314
1315        ## Arguments:
1316
1317        - **xyzr1 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1318            Array of shape (n_beads1, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 1.
1319
1320        - **xyzr2 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1321            Array of shape (n_beads2, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 2.
1322
1323        - **f_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1324            Float dtype for distance calculations. Defaults to np.float64.
1325
1326        ## Returns:
1327
1328        - **np.ndarray**:<br />
1329            Array of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames) containing pairwise distances.
1330        """
1331
1332        coords1 = xyzr1[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1333        coords2 = xyzr2[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1334
1335        radii1 = xyzr1[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1336        radii2 = xyzr2[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1337
1338        n_frames = coords1.shape[1]
1339        n_beads1 = coords1.shape[0]
1340        n_beads2 = coords2.shape[0]
1341
1342        radii_sum = np.zeros((radii1.shape[0], radii2.shape[0]), dtype=f_dtype)
1343        np.add(
1344            radii1[:, None, 0].copy(),
1345            radii2[None, :, 0].copy(),
1346            out=radii_sum,
1347        )
1348
1349        flat_distances = np.zeros((n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames), dtype=f_dtype)
1350
1351        for i in range(n_frames):
1352
1353            temp_dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1354
1355            np.subtract(
1356                cdist(coords1[:, i, :], coords2[:, i, :]),
1357                radii_sum if subtract_radii else 0.0,
1358                out=temp_dmap,
1359                dtype=f_dtype,
1360            )
1361            temp_dmap[temp_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1362
1363            flat_distances[:, i] = temp_dmap.flatten().astype(f_dtype)
1364
1365            del temp_dmap
1366
1367        return flat_distances
1368
1369    @staticmethod
1370    def get_pairwise_maps(
1371        xyzr1: np.ndarray,
1372        xyzr2: np.ndarray,
1373        cutoff: float,
1374        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
1375        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
1376    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
1377        """ Compute pairwise distance and contact maps between two sets of beads
1378        over multiple frames.
1379
1380        NOTE: Pay attention to the size of the input arrays to avoid memory issues.
1381
1382        ## Arguments:
1383
1384        - **xyzr1 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1385            XYZR data for molecule 1, (n_beads1, n_frames, 4).
1386
1387        - **xyzr2 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1388            XYZR data for molecule 2, (n_beads2, n_frames, 4).
1389
1390        - **cutoff (float)**:<br />
1391            Distance cutoff for contact map.
1392
1393        - **f_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1394            Data type for distance map calculations.
1395
1396        - **i_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1397            Data type for contact map calculations.
1398
1399        ## Returns:
1400
1401        - **tuple**:<br />
1402            - **dmap (np.ndarray)**: Distance map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
1403            - **cmap (np.ndarray or None)**: Contact map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
1404        """
1405
1406        coords1 = xyzr1[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1407        coords2 = xyzr2[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1408
1409        radii1 = xyzr1[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1410        radii2 = xyzr2[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1411
1412        n_frames = coords1.shape[1]
1413        n_beads1 = coords1.shape[0]
1414        n_beads2 = coords2.shape[0]
1415
1416        radii_sum = np.zeros((radii1.shape[0], radii2.shape[0]), dtype=f_dtype)
1417        np.add(
1418            radii1[:, None, 0].copy(),
1419            radii2[None, :, 0].copy(),
1420            out=radii_sum,
1421        )
1422
1423        dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1424        cmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=i_dtype)
1425
1426        for i in range(n_frames):
1427
1428            temp_dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1429
1430            np.subtract(
1431                cdist(coords1[:, i, :], coords2[:, i, :]),
1432                radii_sum,
1433                out=temp_dmap,
1434                dtype=f_dtype,
1435            )
1436            temp_dmap[temp_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1437
1438            np.add(
1439                dmap,
1440                temp_dmap,
1441                out=dmap,
1442                dtype=f_dtype,
1443            )
1444
1445            temp_cmap = (temp_dmap <= cutoff).astype(i_dtype)
1446
1447            np.add(
1448                cmap,
1449                temp_cmap,
1450                out=cmap,
1451                dtype=i_dtype,
1452            )
1453
1454            del temp_dmap, temp_cmap
1455
1456        return dmap, cmap

Class to handle pairwise distance and contact maps for given molecule pairs.

PairwiseMaps( mol_pairs: list, xyzr_parser: IMP_Toolbox.analysis.rmf_to_xyzr.XYZRParser, contact_cutoff: float, fraction_cutoff: float, self_interaction: bool = False, f_dtype: numpy.dtype = <class 'numpy.float64'>, i_dtype: numpy.dtype = <class 'numpy.int32'>)

mol_pairs: list

List of enriched molecule pairs. See MoleculePairs class for details.

xyzr_parser: IMP_Toolbox.analysis.rmf_to_xyzr.XYZRParser

XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information.

xyzr_mat: numpy.ndarray

The raw XYZR data as a numpy array of shape (num_beads, num_frames, 4).

xyzr_keys: list

List of bead keys in the format "MOL_COPYIDX_RESNUM" or "MOL_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", corresponding to the rows in xyzr_mat.

molwise_residues: dict

Dictionary mapping molecule names to sets of residue numbers. Format: { "MOL1_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...], "MOL2_COPYIDX": [res1, res2, ...], ... }

molwise_xyzr_keys: dict

Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of bead keys. Format: { "MOL1_COPYIDX": ["MOL1_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...], "MOL2_COPYIDX": ["MOL2_COPYIDX_RESSTART-RESEND", ...], ... }

self_interaction: str

String indicating how to handle self-interactions. Should be one of:

  • "allow_all": allow interactions between all molecule pairs, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
  • "allow_none": disallow interactions between any molecule pairs of the same molecule, including self-pairs and copy pairs.
  • "allow_copies": allow interactions between different copies of the same molecule, but disallow self-pairs. (default)
unique_mols: set

Set of unique molecule names (without copy index) present in the model.

f_dtype: numpy.dtype

The floating point data type to use for the distance and contact maps.

i_dtype: numpy.dtype

The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps.

contact_cutoff: float

The cutoff distance used for binarization of the distance maps, which will be passed to the get_binary_map function if binarization is specified. See get_binary_map() for more details.

fraction_cutoff: float

The cutoff fraction used for binarization of the contact maps, which will be passed to the get_binary_map function if binarization is specified. See get_binary_map() for more details.
