def process_pairwise_maps( self, pairwise_maps: dict, map_type: str, merge_operation: str = 'average', merge_copies: bool = False, binarize_map: bool = False) -> Dict[str, numpy.ndarray]: 
813    def process_pairwise_maps(
814        self,
815        pairwise_maps: dict,
816        map_type: str,
817        merge_operation: str = "average",
818        merge_copies: bool = False,
819        binarize_map: bool = False,
820    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
821        """ Process pairwise distance or contact maps by expanding to residue-level,
822        merging across copies if specified, and binarizing if specified.
823
824        ## Arguments:
825
826        - **pairwise_maps (dict)**:<br />
827            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
828            to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
829
830        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
831            A string indicating the type of maps being processed.
832            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
833
834        - **merge_copies (bool, optional):**:<br />
835            Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the
836            maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps
837            will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the `merge_maps_by_copies`
838            function. If False, the maps will be processed separately for each copy pair.
839
840        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
841            Whether to binarize the maps based on the cutoff. If True, the maps will be
842            converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a contact is
843            defined as present if it is present in any of the copy pairs (if merge_copies
844            is True) or based on the cutoff for each individual map (if merge_copies is False).
845            If False, the maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values.
846
847        ## Returns:
848
849        - **dict**:<br />
850            A dictionary of processed interaction maps per molecule pair.
851        """
852
853        assert map_type in ["dmap", "cmap"], "map_type must be either 'dmap' or 'cmap'"
854
855        ############################################################################
856        # Expand the maps to residue-level for plotting and patch extraction.
857        ############################################################################
858        for pair_name, pairwise_map in pairwise_maps.items():
859
860            pairwise_maps[pair_name] = expand_map_to_residue_level(
861                q_map=pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype),
862                molwise_xyzr_keys=self.molwise_xyzr_keys,
863                pair_name=pair_name
864            )
865
866        ############################################################################
867        # Merge maps across copies if specified, and binarize if specified.
868        ############################################################################
869        if merge_copies:
870
871            pairwise_maps = self.merge_maps_by_copies(
872                pairwise_maps=pairwise_maps,
873                map_type=map_type,
874                operation="or" if binarize_map else merge_operation,
875                binarize_map=binarize_map,
876            )
877
878        else:
879
880            for pair_name, pairwise_map in pairwise_maps.items():
881
882                if binarize_map:
883                    pairwise_maps[pair_name] = get_binary_map(
884                        q_map=pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype),
885                        binarization_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff if map_type=="dmap" else self.fraction_cutoff,
886                        map_type=map_type,
887                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype
888                    )
889
890                else:
891                    pairwise_maps[pair_name] = pairwise_map.astype(self.f_dtype)
892
893        return pairwise_maps

Process pairwise distance or contact maps by expanding to residue-level, merging across copies if specified, and binarizing if specified.

Arguments:

  • pairwise_maps (dict):
    A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX") to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).

  • map_type (str):
    A string indicating the type of maps being processed. Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.

  • merge_copies (bool, optional)::
    Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the merge_maps_by_copies function. If False, the maps will be processed separately for each copy pair.

  • binarize_map (bool, optional)::
    Whether to binarize the maps based on the cutoff. If True, the maps will be converted to binary maps using the get_binary_map function, where a contact is defined as present if it is present in any of the copy pairs (if merge_copies is True) or based on the cutoff for each individual map (if merge_copies is False). If False, the maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values.

Returns:

  • dict:
    A dictionary of processed interaction maps per molecule pair.
def prepare_xyzr_batches( self, frame_batches: List[numpy.ndarray], res_range: Optional[str], mol_name: str) -> Tuple[List[int], List[numpy.ndarray]]: 
895    def prepare_xyzr_batches(
896        self,
897        frame_batches: List[np.ndarray],
898        res_range: Optional[str],
899        mol_name: str
900    ) -> Tuple[List[int], List[np.ndarray]]:
901        """ Prepare batches of XYZR data for the specified molecule and residue range.
902
903        ## Arguments:
904
905        - **frame_batches (List[np.ndarray])**:<br />
906            A list of numpy arrays, where each array contains the frame indices
907            for a batch.
908
909        - **res_range (Optional[str])**:<br />
910            A string specifying the residue range to select for the molecule.
911            Should be in the format "RESSTART-RESEND". If None, all residues for
912            the molecule will be selected.
913
914        - **mol_name (str)**:<br />
915            The name of the molecule for which to prepare the XYZR batches. Should
916            be in the format "MOL_COPYIDX".
917
918        ## Returns:
919
920        - **Tuple[List[int], List[np.ndarray]]**:<br />
921            A tuple containing:
922            - A list of indices corresponding to the selected residues for the
923              molecule.
924            - A list of numpy arrays, where each array contains the XYZR data
925              for the selected residues and frames in the corresponding batch.
926        """
927
928        res_range = (
929            get_res_range_from_key(res_range)
930            if res_range is not None else self.molwise_residues[mol_name]
931        )
932
933        idx = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol_name, res_range, self.xyzr_keys)
934        xyzr = self.xyzr_mat[idx, :, :].astype(self.f_dtype)
935        xyzr_batches = [
936            xyzr[:, f_batch, :].astype(self.f_dtype)
937            for f_batch in frame_batches
938        ]
939
940        del xyzr
941
942        return idx, xyzr_batches

  • mol_name (str):

def merge_maps_by_copies( self, pairwise_maps: dict, map_type: str, operation: str = 'average', binarize_map: bool = False) -> Dict[str, numpy.ndarray]: 
 944    def merge_maps_by_copies(
 945        self,
 946        pairwise_maps: dict,
 947        map_type: str,
 948        operation: str = "average",
 949        binarize_map:bool = False,
 950    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
 951        """ Merge contact or distance maps across copy pairs.
 952
 953        > [!NOTE]
 954        > if the binarize_map flag is set to True,
 955        > the merged map is a binary map where a contact is defined as present if
 956        > it is present in any of the copy pairs.
 957        >
 958        > if the binarize_map flag is set to False,
 959        > the merged map is - average of the distance/contact maps across copy pairs.
 960
 961        ## Arguments:
 962
 963        - **pairwise_maps (dict)**:<br />
 964            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX")
 965            to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 966
 967        - **map_type (str)**:<br />
 968            A string indicating the type of maps being merged.
 969            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
 970
 971        - **operation (str, optional):**:<br />
 972            The operation to use when merging the maps across copy pairs. Should be
 973            either "average" to take the average of the maps across copy pairs or "or"
 974            to take the logical OR of the maps across copy pairs when binarizing.
 975            (default: "average")
 976
 977        - **binarize_map (bool, optional):**:<br />
 978            Whether to binarize the merged maps based on the cutoff.
 979            - If True, the merged maps will be converted to binary maps using the
 980              `get_binary_map` function, where a contact is defined as present
 981               if it is present in any of the copy pairs.
 982            - If False, the merged maps will not be binarized and will retain
 983              their original values (e.g. average distances or contact frequencies).
 984              (default: False)
 985
 986        ## Returns:
 987
 988        - **dict**:<br />
 989            A dictionary mapping merged molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") to
 990            their corresponding merged distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
 991        """
 992
 993        merged_pairwise_maps = defaultdict(list)
 994
 995        def raise_invalid_operation_error(operation):
 996            raise ValueError(f"Invalid operation: {operation}.")
 997
 998        func_ = {
 999            ("average", False): lambda v: np.mean(v, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1000            ("or", True): lambda v: np.logical_or.reduce(v, axis=0).astype(self.i_dtype),
1001            ("min", False): lambda v: np.min(np.stack(v, axis=0), axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1002            ("max", False): lambda v: np.max(np.stack(v, axis=0), axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype),
1003        }.get(
1004            (operation, binarize_map),
1005            lambda v: raise_invalid_operation_error(operation)
1006        )
1007
1008        for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
1009
1010            _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
1011            base1, _, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1012            base2, _, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1013
1014            merged_pair_name = (
1015                f"{base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
1016                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
1017                f"{base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
1018            )
1019
1020            _map = pairwise_maps[pair_name].copy()
1021
1022            if binarize_map is True:
1023                _map = get_binary_map(
1024                    q_map=_map,
1025                    binarization_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff if map_type=="dmap" else self.fraction_cutoff,
1026                    map_type=map_type,
1027                    i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1028                )
1029
1030            merged_pairwise_maps[merged_pair_name].append(_map)
1031
1032        merged_pairwise_maps = {
1033            k: func_(v)
1034            for k, v in merged_pairwise_maps.items()
1035        }
1036
1037        return merged_pairwise_maps

Merge contact or distance maps across copy pairs.

Note

if the binarize_map flag is set to True, the merged map is a binary map where a contact is defined as present if it is present in any of the copy pairs.

if the binarize_map flag is set to False, the merged map is - average of the distance/contact maps across copy pairs.

Arguments:

  • pairwise_maps (dict):
    A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX") to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).

  • map_type (str):
    A string indicating the type of maps being merged. Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.

  • operation (str, optional)::
    The operation to use when merging the maps across copy pairs. Should be either "average" to take the average of the maps across copy pairs or "or" to take the logical OR of the maps across copy pairs when binarizing. (default: "average")

  • binarize_map (bool, optional)::
    Whether to binarize the merged maps based on the cutoff.

    • If True, the merged maps will be converted to binary maps using the get_binary_map function, where a contact is defined as present if it is present in any of the copy pairs.
    • If False, the merged maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values (e.g. average distances or contact frequencies). (default: False)

Returns:

  • dict:
    A dictionary mapping merged molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") to their corresponding merged distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).
def fetch_pairwise_distances( self, output_dir: str, nproc: int, operation: str = 'min', subtract_radii: bool = True, overwrite: bool = False) -> dict:

1051        - **xyzr_mat (np.ndarray)**:<br />

1055        - **xyzr_keys (list)**:<br />
1056            List of strings representing the keys for each bead in the XYZR data.

1058
1059        - **mol_pairs (list)**:<br />
1060            List of tuples, where each tuple contains two strings representing the
1061            names of the molecules in a binding pair, including copy indices and residue range information.
1062                For example:

1064            [
1065                ("ProteinA_copy1_10-50", "ProteinB_copy1_20-60"),
1066                ("ProteinA_copy2_10-50", "ProteinB_copy2_20-60"),
1067                ("ProteinC_copy1_5-30", "ProteinD_copy1_15-45"),
1068                ("ProteinC_copy2_5-30", "ProteinD_copy2_15-45")
1069            ]
1070            ```
1071
1072        - **output_dir (str)**:<br />
1073            Directory to save output distance map files. Each pairwise distance map will
1074            be saved as a text file named "Molecule1_Molecule2_dmap.txt" in this directory.
1075
1076        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1077            Number of processes to use for parallel distance map calculations.
1078
1079        - **f_dtype (np.dtype)**:<br />
1080            Float dtype for distance calculations.
1081
1082        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1083            Whether to overwrite existing distance map files. If False and a distance
1084            map file already exists for a given pair, the function will load the
1085            distance map from the file instead of recalculating it. Defaults to False.
1086
1087        ## Returns:
1088
1089        - **dict**:<br />
1090            Dictionary where keys are pair names formatted as "Molecule1_Molecule2" and
1091            values are arrays of shape (num_frames,) containing the minimum distance
1092            across all bead pairs for each frame.
1093        """
1094
1095        funcs = {
1096            "min": np.min,
1097            "average": np.average,
1098        }
1099
1100        pairwise_dmaps = {}
1101
1102        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), nproc)
1103
1104        for _m1, _m2 in tqdm.tqdm(self.mol_pairs):
1105
1106            _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1107            _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1108
1109            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
1110            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
1111            pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}" # this should include copy idx
1112
1113            dmap_txt = Path(output_dir) / f"{pair_name}_dmap.txt"
1114
1115            if os.path.exists(dmap_txt) and overwrite is False:
1116                pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(
1117                    dmap_txt,
1118                    dtype=self.f_dtype,
1119                )
1120                continue
1121
1122            _idx1, xyzr1_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1123                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1124                res_range=range1,
1125                mol_name=mol1,
1126            )
1127
1128            _idx2, xyzr2_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1129                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1130                res_range=range2,
1131                mol_name=mol2,
1132            )
1133
1134            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1135                futures = [
1136                    executor.submit(
1137                        PairwiseMaps.get_pairwise_distances,
1138                        xyzr1_b,
1139                        xyzr2_b,
1140                        self.f_dtype,
1141                        subtract_radii
1142                    )
1143                    for xyzr1_b, xyzr2_b in zip(xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches)
1144                ]
1145                results = []
1146                for future in tqdm.tqdm(as_completed(futures), total=len(futures)):
1147                    results.append(future.result())
1148
1149            del xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches
1150
1151            dmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros(self.num_frames, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1152
1153            n_frames = 0
1154            for i, flat_dmap_ in enumerate(results):
1155                # from each flattened dmap of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, batch_frames),
1156                # we take the minimum distance across all bead pairs for each frame,
1157                # resulting in an array of shape (batch_frames,)
1158                frame_slice = slice(n_frames, n_frames + flat_dmap_.shape[1])
1159                # dmap_m1_m2[frame_slice] = np.min(flat_dmap_, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype)
1160                dmap_m1_m2[frame_slice] = funcs[operation](flat_dmap_, axis=0).astype(self.f_dtype)
1161                n_frames += flat_dmap_.shape[1]
1162
1163            del results
1164

1166
1167            if not os.path.exists(dmap_txt) or overwrite:
1168                np.savetxt(dmap_txt, dmap_m1_m2, fmt="%.6f")

Fetch pairwise distance maps from XYZR data.

Arguments:

    List of tuples, where each tuple contains two strings representing the names of the molecules in a binding pair, including copy indices and residue range information. For example:

    [
    ("ProteinA_copy1_10-50", "ProteinB_copy1_20-60"),
    ("ProteinA_copy2_10-50", "ProteinB_copy2_20-60"),
    ("ProteinC_copy1_5-30", "ProteinD_copy1_15-45"),
    ("ProteinC_copy2_5-30", "ProteinD_copy2_15-45")
]

  • output_dir (str):
    Directory to save output distance map files. Each pairwise distance map will be saved as a text file named "Molecule1_Molecule2_dmap.txt" in this directory.

    Number of processes to use for parallel distance map calculations.

  • f_dtype (np.dtype):
    Float dtype for distance calculations.

  • overwrite (bool, optional)::
    Whether to overwrite existing distance map files. If False and a distance map file already exists for a given pair, the function will load the distance map from the file instead of recalculating it. Defaults to False.

  • dict:
    Dictionary where keys are pair names formatted as "Molecule1_Molecule2" and values are arrays of shape (num_frames,) containing the minimum distance across all bead pairs for each frame.

1178        """ Fetch pairwise distance and contact maps for specified molecule pairs.
1179
1180        > [!NOTE]
1181        > The selection defined in `mol_pairs` matters here.
1182        > The maps will only be computed for the selected residue ranges.
1183

1187            The directory where interaction maps are saved.

1189        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1190            The number of processes to use for parallel computation.
1191
1192        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1193            Whether to overwrite existing interaction map files. If False, function

1196            current binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if

1200

1205            - pairwise_cmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their
1206            corresponding average contact maps (numpy arrays).

1208
1209        pairwise_dmaps = {}
1210        pairwise_cmaps = {}
1211
1212        # num_frames = self.xyzr_mat.shape[1]
1213        num_beads = self.xyzr_mat.shape[0]
1214        assert self.xyzr_mat.shape[2] == 4, "Expected last dimension of xyzr_mat to be 4 (XYZR)."
1215        assert num_beads == len(self.xyzr_keys), "Number of beads in xyzr_mat does not match length of bead keys."
1216
1217        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), nproc)
1218
1219        for _m1, _m2 in tqdm.tqdm(self.mol_pairs):
1220
1221            pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}"
1222
1223            dmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_dmap.txt"
1224            cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_cmap.txt"
1225
1226            _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
1227            _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
1228
1229            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
1230            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
1231
1232            if (
1233                dmap_file.exists() and cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False
1234            ):
1235
1236                pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file)
1237                pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(dmap_file)
1238                continue
1239
1240            idx1, xyzr1_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1241                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1242                res_range=range1,
1243                mol_name=mol1,
1244            )
1245
1246            idx2, xyzr2_batches = self.prepare_xyzr_batches(
1247                frame_batches=frame_batches,
1248                res_range=range2,
1249                mol_name=mol2,
1250            )
1251
1252            with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1253                futures = [
1254                    executor.submit(
1255                        PairwiseMaps.get_pairwise_maps,
1256                        xyzr1_b,
1257                        xyzr2_b,
1258                        self.contact_cutoff,
1259                        self.f_dtype,
1260                        self.i_dtype
1261                    )
1262                    for xyzr1_b, xyzr2_b in zip(xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches)
1263                ]
1264                results = []
1265                for future in tqdm.tqdm(
1266                    as_completed(futures), total=len(futures)
1267                ):
1268                    results.append(future.result())
1269
1270            del xyzr1_batches, xyzr2_batches
1271
1272            dmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros((len(idx1), len(idx2)), dtype=self.f_dtype)
1273            cmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros((len(idx1), len(idx2)), dtype=self.i_dtype)
1274
1275            for i, (dmap_, cmap_) in enumerate(results):
1276                np.add(dmap_m1_m2, dmap_, out=dmap_m1_m2, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1277                np.add(cmap_m1_m2, cmap_, out=cmap_m1_m2, dtype=self.i_dtype)
1278
1279            del results
1280
1281            pairwise_dmaps[pair_name] = (
1282                dmap_m1_m2.astype(self.f_dtype) / self.f_dtype(self.num_frames)
1283            )
1284            pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = (
1285                cmap_m1_m2.astype(self.i_dtype) / self.f_dtype(self.num_frames)
1286            )
1287
1288            save_map_txt(
1289                q_map=pairwise_dmaps[pair_name],
1290                save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1291                map_name=f"{pair_name}_dmap",
1292                overwrite=overwrite,
1293            )
1294
1295            save_map_txt(
1296                q_map=pairwise_cmaps[pair_name],
1297                save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1298                map_name=f"{pair_name}_cmap",
1299                overwrite=overwrite,
1300            )
1301
1302        del self.xyzr_mat
1303
1304        return pairwise_dmaps, pairwise_cmaps

Fetch pairwise distance and contact maps for specified molecule pairs.

Note

The selection defined in mol_pairs matters here. The maps will only be computed for the selected residue ranges.

Arguments:

  • interaction_map_dir (str):
    The directory where interaction maps are saved.

  • nproc (int):
    The number of processes to use for parallel computation.

  • overwrite (bool, optional)::
    Whether to overwrite existing interaction map files. If False, function will load existing maps from disk if they are available, and skip recomputation. Note that the plots are always overwritten to reflect the current binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if the files already exist.

Returns:

  • tuple:
    A tuple containing two dictionaries:
    • pairwise_dmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") to their corresponding average distance maps (numpy arrays).
    • pairwise_cmaps: A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their corresponding average contact maps (numpy arrays).
@staticmethod
def get_pairwise_distances( xyzr1: numpy.ndarray, xyzr2: numpy.ndarray, f_dtype: numpy.dtype = <class 'numpy.float64'>, subtract_radii: bool = True): 
1306    @staticmethod
1307    def get_pairwise_distances(
1308        xyzr1: np.ndarray,
1309        xyzr2: np.ndarray,
1310        f_dtype: np.dtype=np.float64,
1311        subtract_radii: bool=True,
1312    ):
1313        """ Given two arrays of XYZR, return all pairwise distances.
1314
1315        ## Arguments:
1316
1317        - **xyzr1 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1318            Array of shape (n_beads1, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 1.
1319
1320        - **xyzr2 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1321            Array of shape (n_beads2, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 2.
1322
1323        - **f_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1324            Float dtype for distance calculations. Defaults to np.float64.
1325
1326        ## Returns:
1327
1328        - **np.ndarray**:<br />
1329            Array of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames) containing pairwise distances.
1330        """
1331
1332        coords1 = xyzr1[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1333        coords2 = xyzr2[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1334
1335        radii1 = xyzr1[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1336        radii2 = xyzr2[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1337
1338        n_frames = coords1.shape[1]
1339        n_beads1 = coords1.shape[0]
1340        n_beads2 = coords2.shape[0]
1341
1342        radii_sum = np.zeros((radii1.shape[0], radii2.shape[0]), dtype=f_dtype)
1343        np.add(
1344            radii1[:, None, 0].copy(),
1345            radii2[None, :, 0].copy(),
1346            out=radii_sum,
1347        )
1348
1349        flat_distances = np.zeros((n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames), dtype=f_dtype)
1350
1351        for i in range(n_frames):
1352
1353            temp_dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1354
1355            np.subtract(
1356                cdist(coords1[:, i, :], coords2[:, i, :]),
1357                radii_sum if subtract_radii else 0.0,
1358                out=temp_dmap,
1359                dtype=f_dtype,
1360            )
1361            temp_dmap[temp_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1362
1363            flat_distances[:, i] = temp_dmap.flatten().astype(f_dtype)
1364
1365            del temp_dmap
1366
1367        return flat_distances

Given two arrays of XYZR, return all pairwise distances.

Arguments:

  • xyzr1 (np.ndarray):
    Array of shape (n_beads1, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 1.

  • xyzr2 (np.ndarray):
    Array of shape (n_beads2, n_frames, 4) containing XYZR data for molecule 2.

  • f_dtype (np.dtype, optional)::
    Float dtype for distance calculations. Defaults to np.float64.

Returns:

  • np.ndarray:
    Array of shape (n_beads1*n_beads2, n_frames) containing pairwise distances.
@staticmethod
def get_pairwise_maps( xyzr1: numpy.ndarray, xyzr2: numpy.ndarray, cutoff: float, f_dtype: numpy.dtype = <class 'numpy.float64'>, i_dtype: numpy.dtype = <class 'numpy.int32'>) -> tuple[numpy.ndarray, numpy.ndarray]: 
1369    @staticmethod
1370    def get_pairwise_maps(
1371        xyzr1: np.ndarray,
1372        xyzr2: np.ndarray,
1373        cutoff: float,
1374        f_dtype: np.dtype = np.float64,
1375        i_dtype: np.dtype = np.int32,
1376    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
1377        """ Compute pairwise distance and contact maps between two sets of beads
1378        over multiple frames.
1379
1380        NOTE: Pay attention to the size of the input arrays to avoid memory issues.
1381
1382        ## Arguments:
1383
1384        - **xyzr1 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1385            XYZR data for molecule 1, (n_beads1, n_frames, 4).
1386
1387        - **xyzr2 (np.ndarray)**:<br />
1388            XYZR data for molecule 2, (n_beads2, n_frames, 4).
1389
1390        - **cutoff (float)**:<br />
1391            Distance cutoff for contact map.
1392
1393        - **f_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1394            Data type for distance map calculations.
1395
1396        - **i_dtype (np.dtype, optional):**:<br />
1397            Data type for contact map calculations.
1398
1399        ## Returns:
1400
1401        - **tuple**:<br />
1402            - **dmap (np.ndarray)**: Distance map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
1403            - **cmap (np.ndarray or None)**: Contact map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
1404        """
1405
1406        coords1 = xyzr1[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1407        coords2 = xyzr2[:, :, :3].astype(f_dtype)
1408
1409        radii1 = xyzr1[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1410        radii2 = xyzr2[:, :, 3].astype(f_dtype)
1411
1412        n_frames = coords1.shape[1]
1413        n_beads1 = coords1.shape[0]
1414        n_beads2 = coords2.shape[0]
1415
1416        radii_sum = np.zeros((radii1.shape[0], radii2.shape[0]), dtype=f_dtype)
1417        np.add(
1418            radii1[:, None, 0].copy(),
1419            radii2[None, :, 0].copy(),
1420            out=radii_sum,
1421        )
1422
1423        dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1424        cmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=i_dtype)
1425
1426        for i in range(n_frames):
1427
1428            temp_dmap = np.zeros((n_beads1, n_beads2), dtype=f_dtype)
1429
1430            np.subtract(
1431                cdist(coords1[:, i, :], coords2[:, i, :]),
1432                radii_sum,
1433                out=temp_dmap,
1434                dtype=f_dtype,
1435            )
1436            temp_dmap[temp_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1437
1438            np.add(
1439                dmap,
1440                temp_dmap,
1441                out=dmap,
1442                dtype=f_dtype,
1443            )
1444
1445            temp_cmap = (temp_dmap <= cutoff).astype(i_dtype)
1446
1447            np.add(
1448                cmap,
1449                temp_cmap,
1450                out=cmap,
1451                dtype=i_dtype,
1452            )
1453
1454            del temp_dmap, temp_cmap
1455
1456        return dmap, cmap

Compute pairwise distance and contact maps between two sets of beads over multiple frames.

NOTE: Pay attention to the size of the input arrays to avoid memory issues.

Arguments:

  • xyzr1 (np.ndarray):
    XYZR data for molecule 1, (n_beads1, n_frames, 4).

  • xyzr2 (np.ndarray):
    XYZR data for molecule 2, (n_beads2, n_frames, 4).

  • cutoff (float):
    Distance cutoff for contact map.

  • f_dtype (np.dtype, optional)::
    Data type for distance map calculations.

  • i_dtype (np.dtype, optional)::
    Data type for contact map calculations.

Returns:

  • tuple:
    • dmap (np.ndarray): Distance map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).
    • cmap (np.ndarray or None): Contact map of shape (n_beads1, n_beads2).

1513        self,

1541    @staticmethod
1542    def contact_map_worker(
1543        batch_xyz: np.ndarray,
1544        radii_sum: np.ndarray,
1545        contact_cutoff: float,
1546        grouped_mol_pairs: Dict[str, set],
1547        merge_copies: bool,
1548        f_dtype: np.dtype,
1549        i_dtype: np.dtype,
1550        molwise_xyzr_keys: dict,
1551        molwise_residues: dict,
1552        xyzr_keys: list,
1553    ) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
1554
1555        batchwise_cmaps = {}
1556
1557        for frame_id in range(batch_xyz.shape[1]):
1558            pairwise_cmaps = {}
1559            frame_coords = batch_xyz[:, frame_id, :].astype(f_dtype)
1560            diffs = pdist(frame_coords)
1561            frame_dmap = squareform(diffs, checks=False).astype(f_dtype)
1562            np.subtract(
1563                frame_dmap,
1564                radii_sum,
1565                out=frame_dmap,
1566                dtype=f_dtype,
1567            )
1568            frame_dmap[frame_dmap < 0.0] = 0.0
1569            frame_cmap = (frame_dmap <= contact_cutoff).astype(i_dtype)
1570
1571            for base_pair, copy_pairs in grouped_mol_pairs.items():
1572
1573                for _m1, _m2 in copy_pairs:
1574
1575                    pair_name, pair_cmap = PairwiseContactMaps.extract_copy_pair_contact_map(
1576                        frame_cmap=frame_cmap,
1577                        m1=_m1,
1578                        m2=_m2,
1579                        molwise_xyzr_keys=molwise_xyzr_keys,
1580                        molwise_residues=molwise_residues,
1581                        xyzr_keys=xyzr_keys,
1582                        merge_copies=merge_copies,
1583                    )
1584
1585                    if pair_name not in pairwise_cmaps:
1586                        cmap_m1_m2 = np.zeros_like(pair_cmap, dtype=i_dtype)
1587
1588                    np.logical_or(
1589                        pair_cmap,
1590                        cmap_m1_m2,
1591                        out=cmap_m1_m2,
1592                    )
1593                    pairwise_cmaps[pair_name] = cmap_m1_m2
1594
1595                    if merge_copies is True:
1596                        continue
1597
1598                    PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1599                        cmaps_to_update=batchwise_cmaps,
1600                        cmaps_to_add=pairwise_cmaps,
1601                        pair_name=pair_name,
1602                        i_dtype=i_dtype,
1603                    )
1604
1605                if merge_copies is False:
1606                    continue
1607
1608                PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1609                    cmaps_to_update=batchwise_cmaps,
1610                    cmaps_to_add=pairwise_cmaps,
1611                    pair_name=base_pair,
1612                    i_dtype=i_dtype,
1613                )
1614
1615        return batchwise_cmaps
1616
1617    @staticmethod
1618    def update_cmaps(
1619        cmaps_to_update,
1620        cmaps_to_add,
1621        pair_name,
1622        i_dtype=np.int32,
1623    ):
1624
1625        if pair_name not in cmaps_to_update:
1626            cmaps_to_update[pair_name] = np.zeros_like(cmaps_to_add[pair_name], dtype=i_dtype)
1627
1628        np.add(
1629            cmaps_to_add[pair_name].astype(i_dtype),
1630            cmaps_to_update[pair_name].astype(i_dtype),
1631            out=cmaps_to_update[pair_name], dtype=i_dtype
1632        )
1633
1634    @staticmethod
1635    def extract_copy_pair_contact_map(
1636        frame_cmap,
1637        m1,
1638        m2,
1639        molwise_xyzr_keys,
1640        molwise_residues,
1641        xyzr_keys,
1642        merge_copies=False,
1643    ):
1644
1645        _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m1).groups()
1646        _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, m2).groups()
1647
1648        pair_name = f"{m1}{PAIR_SEP}{m2}"
1649
1650        mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m1, only_base=False)
1651        mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(m2, only_base=False)
1652
1653        res_range1 = (
1654            get_res_range_from_key(range1)
1655            if range1 is not None else molwise_residues[mol1]
1656        )
1657
1658        idx1 = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol1, res_range1, xyzr_keys)
1659
1660        res_range2 = (
1661            get_res_range_from_key(range2)
1662            if range2 is not None else molwise_residues[mol2]
1663        )
1664
1665        idx2 = XYZRParser.get_bead_indices(mol2, res_range2, xyzr_keys)
1666
1667        pair_cmap = frame_cmap[np.ix_(idx1, idx2)]
1668        pair_cmap = expand_map_to_residue_level(
1669            q_map=pair_cmap,
1670            molwise_xyzr_keys=molwise_xyzr_keys,
1671            pair_name=pair_name,
1672        )
1673
1674        if merge_copies:
1675            pair_name = (
1676                f"{_base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
1677                PAIR_SEP +
1678                f"{_base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
1679            )
1680
1681        return pair_name, pair_cmap
1682
1683    def compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1684        self,
1685        nproc: int,
1686        interaction_map_dir: str,
1687        overwrite: bool = False,
1688    ) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
1689
1690        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), args.nproc)
1691
1692        radii_data = self.xyzr_mat[:, 0, 3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1693        radii_sum = np.zeros(
1694            (radii_data.shape[0], radii_data.shape[0]), dtype=self.f_dtype
1695        )
1696        np.add(
1697            radii_data[:, None].copy(),
1698            radii_data[None, :].copy(),
1699            out=radii_sum,
1700        )
1701
1702        xyz_data = self.xyzr_mat[:, :, :3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1703        batchwise_xyz = [
1704            xyz_data[:, frame_batch, :3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1705            for frame_batch in frame_batches
1706        ]
1707
1708        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1709            futures = [
1710                executor.submit(
1711                    PairwiseContactMaps.contact_map_worker,
1712                    batch_xyz=xyz_batch,
1713                    radii_sum=radii_sum,
1714                    contact_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff,
1715                    grouped_mol_pairs=self.grouped_mol_pairs,
1716                    merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1717                    f_dtype=self.f_dtype,
1718                    i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1719                    molwise_xyzr_keys=self.molwise_xyzr_keys,
1720                    molwise_residues=self.molwise_residues,
1721                    xyzr_keys=self.xyzr_keys,
1722                )
1723                for xyz_batch in batchwise_xyz
1724            ]
1725            for future in as_completed(futures):
1726
1727                batch_cmaps = future.result()
1728
1729                for pair_name in batch_cmaps.keys():
1730
1731                    PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1732                        cmaps_to_update=self.modelwise_cmaps,
1733                        cmaps_to_add=batch_cmaps,
1734                        pair_name=pair_name,
1735                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1736                    )
1737                    save_map_txt(
1738                        q_map=self.modelwise_cmaps[pair_name],
1739                        save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1740                        map_name=f"{pair_name}_cmap",
1741                        overwrite=overwrite,
1742                    )
1743
1744        self.modelwise_cmaps = {
1745            pair_name: cmap / self.num_frames
1746            for pair_name, cmap in self.modelwise_cmaps.items()
1747        }
1748
1749    def fetch_pairwise_contact_maps(
1750        self,
1751        interaction_map_dir: str,
1752        nproc: int,
1753        overwrite: bool = False,
1754    ) -> dict:
1755
1756        # try to load existing maps from disk if available and overwrite is False
1757        if self.merge_copies is True:
1758            for base_pair, copy_pairs in self.grouped_mol_pairs.items():
1759
1760                cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{base_pair}_cmap.txt"
1761                if cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False:
1762                    print(f"Loading existing contact map for {base_pair} from {cmap_file}.")
1763                    self.modelwise_cmaps[base_pair] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1764                else:
1765                    self.compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1766                        nproc=nproc,
1767                        interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1768                        overwrite=overwrite,
1769                    )
1770                    break
1771        else:
1772            for _m1, _m2 in self.mol_pairs:
1773
1774                pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}"
1775                cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_cmap.txt"
1776
1777                if cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False:
1778                    print(f"Loading existing contact map for {base_pair} from {cmap_file}.")
1779                    self.modelwise_cmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1780                else:
1781                    self.compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1782                        nproc=nproc,
1783                        interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1784                        overwrite=overwrite,
1785                    )
1786                    break
1787
1788        return self.modelwise_cmaps

1676                f"{_base1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
1677                PAIR_SEP +
1678                f"{_base2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
1679            )
1680
1681        return pair_name, pair_cmap
def compute_pairwise_contact_maps( self, nproc: int, interaction_map_dir: str, overwrite: bool = False) -> tuple[dict, dict]: 
1683    def compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1684        self,
1685        nproc: int,
1686        interaction_map_dir: str,
1687        overwrite: bool = False,
1688    ) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
1689
1690        frame_batches = np.array_split(np.arange(self.num_frames), args.nproc)
1691
1692        radii_data = self.xyzr_mat[:, 0, 3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1693        radii_sum = np.zeros(
1694            (radii_data.shape[0], radii_data.shape[0]), dtype=self.f_dtype
1695        )
1696        np.add(
1697            radii_data[:, None].copy(),
1698            radii_data[None, :].copy(),
1699            out=radii_sum,
1700        )
1701
1702        xyz_data = self.xyzr_mat[:, :, :3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1703        batchwise_xyz = [
1704            xyz_data[:, frame_batch, :3].astype(self.f_dtype)
1705            for frame_batch in frame_batches
1706        ]
1707
1708        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc) as executor:
1709            futures = [
1710                executor.submit(
1711                    PairwiseContactMaps.contact_map_worker,
1712                    batch_xyz=xyz_batch,
1713                    radii_sum=radii_sum,
1714                    contact_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff,
1715                    grouped_mol_pairs=self.grouped_mol_pairs,
1716                    merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1717                    f_dtype=self.f_dtype,
1718                    i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1719                    molwise_xyzr_keys=self.molwise_xyzr_keys,
1720                    molwise_residues=self.molwise_residues,
1721                    xyzr_keys=self.xyzr_keys,
1722                )
1723                for xyz_batch in batchwise_xyz
1724            ]
1725            for future in as_completed(futures):
1726
1727                batch_cmaps = future.result()
1728
1729                for pair_name in batch_cmaps.keys():
1730
1731                    PairwiseContactMaps.update_cmaps(
1732                        cmaps_to_update=self.modelwise_cmaps,
1733                        cmaps_to_add=batch_cmaps,
1734                        pair_name=pair_name,
1735                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
1736                    )
1737                    save_map_txt(
1738                        q_map=self.modelwise_cmaps[pair_name],
1739                        save_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1740                        map_name=f"{pair_name}_cmap",
1741                        overwrite=overwrite,
1742                    )
1743
1744        self.modelwise_cmaps = {
1745            pair_name: cmap / self.num_frames
1746            for pair_name, cmap in self.modelwise_cmaps.items()
1747        }
def fetch_pairwise_contact_maps( self, interaction_map_dir: str, nproc: int, overwrite: bool = False) -> dict: 
1749    def fetch_pairwise_contact_maps(
1750        self,
1751        interaction_map_dir: str,
1752        nproc: int,
1753        overwrite: bool = False,
1754    ) -> dict:
1755
1756        # try to load existing maps from disk if available and overwrite is False
1757        if self.merge_copies is True:
1758            for base_pair, copy_pairs in self.grouped_mol_pairs.items():
1759
1760                cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{base_pair}_cmap.txt"
1761                if cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False:
1762                    print(f"Loading existing contact map for {base_pair} from {cmap_file}.")
1763                    self.modelwise_cmaps[base_pair] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1764                else:
1765                    self.compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1766                        nproc=nproc,
1767                        interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1768                        overwrite=overwrite,
1769                    )
1770                    break
1771        else:
1772            for _m1, _m2 in self.mol_pairs:
1773
1774                pair_name = f"{_m1}{PAIR_SEP}{_m2}"
1775                cmap_file = Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"{pair_name}_cmap.txt"
1776
1777                if cmap_file.exists() and overwrite is False:
1778                    print(f"Loading existing contact map for {base_pair} from {cmap_file}.")
1779                    self.modelwise_cmaps[pair_name] = np.loadtxt(cmap_file, dtype=self.f_dtype)
1780                else:
1781                    self.compute_pairwise_contact_maps(
1782                        nproc=nproc,
1783                        interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1784                        overwrite=overwrite,
1785                    )
1786                    break
1787
1788        return self.modelwise_cmaps
class Interaction: 
1790class Interaction:
1791    """ Class for computing interaction maps for selected molecule pairs."""
1792
1793    xyzr_parser: XYZRParser
1794    """ XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information. """
1795
1796    molwise_residues: dict
1797    """ Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of residue numbers. Format: {
1798        "MOL1": [residue numbers],
1799        "MOL2": [residue numbers],
1800        ...
1801    } """
1802
1803    contact_cutoff: float
1804    """ The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be
1805    passed to the `get_binary_map` function if binarization is specified.
1806    See :func:`get_binary_map` for more details.
1807    """
1808
1809    fraction_cutoff: float
1810    """ The cutoff for the fraction of frames in which a contact is present, used for
1811    binarization of the contact maps. This will be passed to the `get_binary_map`
1812    function if binarization of contact maps is specified. See :func:`get_binary_map`
1813    for more details.
1814    """
1815
1816    f_dtype: np.dtype
1817    """ The floating point data type to use for the distance/contact maps. """
1818
1819    i_dtype: np.dtype
1820    """ The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps. """
1821
1822    merge_copies: bool
1823    """ Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the
1824    maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps
1825    will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the `merge_maps_by_copies`
1826    function. If False, the maps will be treated separately for each copy pair.
1827    """
1828
1829    sel_mol_pairs: list
1830    """ List of selected molecule pairs based on the input selection. See
1831    `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
1832
1833    mol_pairs: list
1834    """ List of all molecule pairs. See `MoleculePairs` class for details."""
1835
1836    def __init__(
1837        self,

1846    ):
1847
1848        if not xyzr_parser.is_setup:

1853
1854        self.contact_cutoff = contact_cutoff
1855        self.fraction_cutoff = fraction_cutoff
1856        self.f_dtype = f_dtype
1857        self.i_dtype = i_dtype

1859
1860        sel_mol_pair_handler = MoleculePairs(
1861            xyzr_parser=xyzr_parser,

1864        )

1874        )

1876

1887        self.pairwise_maps_handler = PairwiseMaps(
1888            mol_pairs=self.mol_pairs,

1890            contact_cutoff=self.contact_cutoff,
1891            fraction_cutoff=self.fraction_cutoff,

1897    def compute_interaction_maps(
1898        self,
1899        interaction_map_dir: str,
1900        nproc: int,
1901        overwrite: bool = False,
1902        binarize_dmap: bool = False,
1903        binarize_cmap: bool = False,
1904    ) -> None:
1905        """ Compute pairwise distance and contact maps for the selected molecule pairs.
1906
1907        ## Arguments:
1908
1909        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
1910            The directory where the computed interaction maps will be saved.
1911
1912        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1913            The number of processes to use for parallel computation of the maps.
1914
1915        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1916            Whether to overwrite existing map files in the interaction_map_dir. If False,
1917            the function will load existing maps from disk if they are available, and skip
1918            recomputation. Note that the plots are always overwritten to reflect the current
1919            binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if the files already exist.
1920
1921        - **binarize_dmap (bool, optional):**:<br />
1922            Whether to binarize the distance maps based on the cutoff. If True, the distance
1923            maps will be converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a
1924            contact is defined as present if the distance is less than or equal to the cutoff.
1925            If False, the distance maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values
1926            (e.g. average distances). (default: False)
1927
1928        - **binarize_cmap (bool, optional):**:<br />
1929            Whether to binarize the contact maps based on the cutoff. If True, the contact maps
1930            will be converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a contact
1931            is defined as present if the contact frequency is greater than or equal to the cutoff.
1932            If False, the contact maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values
1933            (e.g. average contact frequencies). (default: False)
1934        """
1935        (
1936            pairwise_dmaps,
1937            pairwise_cmaps
1938        ) = self.pairwise_maps_handler.fetch_pairwise_maps(
1939            interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1940            nproc=nproc,
1941            overwrite=overwrite,
1942        )
1943
1944        self.pairwise_dmaps = self.pairwise_maps_handler.process_pairwise_maps(
1945            pairwise_maps=pairwise_dmaps,
1946            map_type="dmap",
1947            merge_operation="average",
1948            merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1949            binarize_map=binarize_dmap,
1950        )
1951
1952        self.pairwise_cmaps = self.pairwise_maps_handler.process_pairwise_maps(
1953            pairwise_maps=pairwise_cmaps,
1954            map_type="cmap",
1955            merge_operation="max",
1956            merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1957            binarize_map=binarize_cmap,
1958        )
1959
1960        if self.merge_copies:
1961            self.xyzr_parser.merge_residue_selection_by_copies()
1962            self.molwise_residues = self.xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
1963
1964        self.map_slices = self.generate_map_slices(
1965            pairwise_keys=list(self.pairwise_dmaps.keys()),
1966        )
1967

1988
1989    def generate_map_slices(
1990        self,
1991        pairwise_keys: list,
1992    ) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]]:
1993        """ Generate a dictionary of slice names and their corresponding residue
1994        ranges for each molecule pair.
1995
1996        ## Arguments:
1997
1998        - **pairwise_keys (list)**:<br />
1999            A list of molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") corresponding to the
2000            keys in the pairwise_maps dictionary. This is used to ensure that the
2001            generated slice names are consistent with the keys in the pairwise_maps
2002            dictionary, and to filter out any selected molecule pairs that do not have
2003            corresponding maps.
2004
2005        ## Returns:
2006
2007        - **dict**:<br />
2008            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to dictionaries of slice names and
2009            their corresponding residue ranges. Format:
2010            {
2011                "MOL1:MOL2": {
2012                    "slice_name1": {
2013                        "s1": start residue number for mol1,
2014                        "e1": end residue number for mol1,
2015                        "s2": start residue number for mol2,
2016                        "e2": end residue number for mol2,
2017                    },
2018                    "slice_name2": {
2019                        ...
2020                    },
2021                    ...
2022                },
2023                ...
2024            }
2025        """
2026
2027        map_slices = {k: {} for k in pairwise_keys}
2028
2029        for _m1, _m2 in self.sel_mol_pairs:
2030
2031            _base1, _cp_idx1, sel1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
2032            _base2, _cp_idx2, sel2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
2033
2034            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=self.merge_copies)
2035            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=self.merge_copies)
2036
2037            range1 = f"{min(self.molwise_residues[mol1])}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{max(self.molwise_residues[mol1])}"
2038            range2 = f"{min(self.molwise_residues[mol2])}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{max(self.molwise_residues[mol2])}"
2039
2040            pair_name = (
2041                f"{mol1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
2042                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2043                f"{mol2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
2044            )
2045
2046            if pair_name not in pairwise_keys:
2047                print(f"Warning: {pair_name} not found in computed maps. Skipping.")
2048                continue
2049
2050            s1, e1 = get_res_range_from_key(sel1)[0], get_res_range_from_key(sel1)[-1]
2051            s2, e2 = get_res_range_from_key(sel2)[0], get_res_range_from_key(sel2)[-1]
2052
2053            slice_name = (
2054                f"{mol1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{s1}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{e1}" +
2055                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2056                f"{mol2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{s2}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{e2}"
2057            )
2058
2059            map_slices[pair_name][slice_name] = {
2060                "s1": int(s1),
2061                "e1": int(e1),
2062                "s2": int(s2),
2063                "e2": int(e2),
2064            }
2065
2066        return map_slices
2067
2068    def save_output(
2069        self,
2070        pairwise_maps,
2071        interaction_map_dir,
2072        nproc,
2073        cutoff,
2074        binarize_map,
2075        map_type,
2076        output_type: str = "patches+plots",
2077        plotting_lib: str = "matplotlib",
2078    ):
2079        """ Save the processed interaction maps as plots and/or patches.
2080
2081        ## Arguments:
2082
2083        - **pairwise_maps (_type_)**:<br />
2084            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their corresponding distance
2085            or contact maps (numpy arrays).
2086
2087        - **interaction_map_dir (_type_)**:<br />
2088            The directory where the output maps and plots will be saved.
2089
2090        - **nproc (_type_)**:<br />
2091            The number of processes to use for parallel processing when saving the
2092            maps and plots.
2093
2094        - **cutoff (_type_)**:<br />
2095            The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be
2096            included in the plot title and colorbar label. See :func:`get_binary_map`
2097            for more details.
2098
2099        - **binarize_map (_type_)**:<br />
2100            Whether to binarize the maps before saving and plotting. If True, the maps
2101            will be converted to binary maps based on the cutoff value before saving
2102            and plotting.
2103
2104        - **map_type (_type_)**:<br />
2105            A string indicating the type of maps being saved and plotted.
2106            Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.
2107
2108        - **output_type (str, optional):**:<br />
2109            A string indicating the type of output to save. Can be either "patches",
2110            "plots", or "patches+plots".
2111            - If "patches", only the patches will be saved as csv files.
2112            - If "plots", only the plots will be saved as png files.
2113            - If "patches+plots", both the patches and plots will be saved.
2114
2115        - **plotting_lib (str, optional):**:<br />
2116            The plotting library to use for generating the plots. Can be either
2117            "matplotlib" or "plotly". Default is "matplotlib".
2118        """
2119
2120        output_types = output_type.split("+")
2121        assert all([ot in ["patches", "plots"] for ot in output_types]), (
2122            f"Invalid output_type: {output_type}. Expected 'patches', 'plots', or 'patches+plots'."
2123        )
2124        nproc = min(nproc, len(pairwise_maps), 20)
2125        executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc)
2126
2127        if "plots" in output_types:
2128            for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
2129                executor.submit(
2130                    Interaction.plot_map,
2131                    pairwise_maps[pair_name],
2132                    pair_name,
2133                    interaction_map_dir,
2134                    map_type,
2135                    cutoff,
2136                    self.molwise_residues,
2137                    self.map_slices[pair_name],
2138                    plotting_lib,
2139                    binarize_map,
2140                )
2141
2142        if "patches" in output_types:
2143            if not binarize_map:
2144                pairwise_maps = {
2145                    pair_name: get_binary_map(
2146                        q_map=pairwise_maps[pair_name].astype(self.f_dtype),
2147                        binarization_cutoff=cutoff,
2148                        map_type=map_type,
2149                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
2150                    )
2151                    for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys()
2152                }
2153
2154            for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
2155
2156                executor.submit(
2157                    Interaction.matrix_patches_worker,
2158                    pairwise_maps[pair_name].astype(self.i_dtype),
2159                    pair_name,
2160                    interaction_map_dir,
2161                )
2162
2163        executor.shutdown(wait=False)
2164        print(f"Saved {map_type} maps and plots to {interaction_map_dir}")
2165
2166    @staticmethod
2167    def matrix_patches_worker(
2168        cmap: npt.NDArray[np.integer],
2169        pair_name: str,
2170        interaction_map_dir: str,
2171    ) -> None:
2172        """ Extract interacting patches from the contact map and save them as csvs.
2173
2174        ## Arguments:
2175
2176        - **cmap (npt.NDArray[np.integer])**:<br />
2177            The binary contact map from which to extract patches.
2178
2179        - **pair_name (str)**:<br />
2180            The name of the molecule pair corresponding to the contact map (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2").
2181
2182        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
2183            The directory where the patch files will be saved.
2184        """
2185
2186        _m1, _m2 = pair_name.split(PAIR_SEP)
2187        _base1, _cp_idx1, range1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
2188        _base2, _cp_idx2, range2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
2189        mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=False)
2190        mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=False)
2191
2192        assert all([range1 is not None, range2 is not None]), (
2193            f"Invalid format for molecule pair: {(_m1, _m2)}. "\
2194            "Expected format: MOL_COPYIDX:RESSTART-RESEND"
2195        )
2196
2197        # cheap trick to avoid df.groupby() error
2198        # `df.grouby()` will fail if row_obj and col_obj are the same
2199        if mol1 == mol2:
2200            mol1 += "-1"
2201            mol2 += "-2"
2202
2203        region_of_interest = {
2204            mol1: [
2205                get_res_range_from_key(range1)[0],
2206                get_res_range_from_key(range1)[1]
2207            ],
2208            mol2: [
2209                get_res_range_from_key(range2)[0],
2210                get_res_range_from_key(range2)[1]
2211            ]
2212        }
2213
2214        if len(np.unique(cmap)) == 1 and np.unique(cmap)[0] == 0:
2215            # print(f"No contacts found for {pair_name}, skipping patches.")
2216            return None
2217
2218        matrix_patches = MatrixPatches(
2219            matrix=cmap,
2220            row_obj=mol1,
2221            col_obj=mol2,
2222        )
2223
2224        patches_df = matrix_patches.get_patches_from_matrix()
2225
2226        ch1_p = [
2227            np.array(list(patch)) + region_of_interest[mol1][0]
2228            for patch in patches_df[mol1].tolist()
2229        ]
2230        ch2_p = [
2231            np.array(list(patch)) + region_of_interest[mol2][0]
2232            for patch in patches_df[mol2].tolist()
2233        ]
2234
2235        patches = {
2236            patch_idx: {
2237                mol1: ch1_patch,
2238                mol2: ch2_patch,
2239            } for patch_idx, (ch1_patch, ch2_patch) in enumerate(zip(ch1_p, ch2_p))
2240        }
2241
2242        if len(patches) > 0:
2243
2244            pair_name = (
2245                f"{mol1.replace('-1', '')}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
2246                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2247                f"{mol2.replace('-2', '')}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
2248            )
2249
2250            save_map(
2251                contact_map=cmap,
2252                avg_contact_probs_mat=None,
2253                patches=patches,
2254                chain1=mol1,
2255                chain2=mol2,
2256                p1_name=mol1,
2257                p2_name=mol2,
2258                p1_region=region_of_interest[mol1],
2259                p2_region=region_of_interest[mol2],
2260                out_file=Path(interaction_map_dir) / f"patches_{pair_name}.png",
2261                save_plot=False,
2262                verbose=False,

2446    @staticmethod
2447    def extract_interface_residues_from_patches(
2448        interacting_patches_csvs: list[str],
2449    ):
2450        """ Extract interface residue information from interaction map patch CSV files.
2451
2452        ## Arguments:
2453
2454        - **interacting_patches_csvs (str)**:<br />
2455            A list of paths to CSV files containing the interacting patches
2456            extracted from the contact maps. Each CSV file should have columns
2457            corresponding to the molecule names (e.g. "MOL1", "MOL2")
2458
2459        ## Returns:
2460
2461        - **dict**:<br />
2462            A dictionary mapping interface names to sets of residue pairs.
2463            The keys are interface names in the format "Protein1_Protein2", and the
2464            values are sets of tuples, where each tuple contains the residue ranges
2465            for the interacting residues from the two proteins (e.g.,
2466            ("res1_start-res1_end", "res2_start-res2_end")).
2467        """
2468
2469        interface_dict = defaultdict(list)
2470
2471        for patches_csv_path in interacting_patches_csvs:
2472
2473            patches_df = pd.read_csv(patches_csv_path, header=0)
2474            prot1_n, prot2_n = list(patches_df.columns)
2475            if "_" in prot1_n:
2476                _prot1_n = prot1_n.split("_")[0]
2477            if "_" in prot2_n:
2478                _prot2_n = prot2_n.split("_")[0]
2479
2480            interface_name = f"{_prot1_n.split("-")[0]}_{_prot2_n.split("-")[0]}"
2481            interface_dict[interface_name] = set()
2482
2483            for _, row in patches_df.iterrows():
2484                interface_dict[interface_name].add((row[prot1_n], row[prot2_n]))
2485
2486        return interface_dict

xyzr_parser: IMP_Toolbox.analysis.rmf_to_xyzr.XYZRParser

XYZRParser object containing the parsed XYZR data and related information.

molwise_residues: dict

Dictionary mapping molecule names to lists of residue numbers. Format: { "MOL1": [residue numbers], "MOL2": [residue numbers], ... }

contact_cutoff: float

The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be passed to the get_binary_map function if binarization is specified. See get_binary_map() for more details.

fraction_cutoff: float

The cutoff for the fraction of frames in which a contact is present, used for binarization of the contact maps. This will be passed to the get_binary_map function if binarization of contact maps is specified. See get_binary_map() for more details.

f_dtype: numpy.dtype

The floating point data type to use for the distance/contact maps.

i_dtype: numpy.dtype

The integer data type to use for the binary contact maps.

merge_copies: bool

Whether to merge molecule copies when processing the maps. If True, the maps will be merged across copy pairs (e.g. "MOL1_COPYIDX:MOL2_COPYIDX" maps will be merged into a single "MOL1:MOL2" map) using the merge_maps_by_copies function. If False, the maps will be treated separately for each copy pair.

sel_mol_pairs: list

List of selected molecule pairs based on the input selection. See MoleculePairs class for details.

mol_pairs: list

List of all molecule pairs. See MoleculePairs class for details.

def compute_interaction_maps( self, interaction_map_dir: str, nproc: int, overwrite: bool = False, binarize_dmap: bool = False, binarize_cmap: bool = False) -> None: 
1897    def compute_interaction_maps(
1898        self,
1899        interaction_map_dir: str,
1900        nproc: int,
1901        overwrite: bool = False,
1902        binarize_dmap: bool = False,
1903        binarize_cmap: bool = False,
1904    ) -> None:
1905        """ Compute pairwise distance and contact maps for the selected molecule pairs.
1906
1907        ## Arguments:
1908
1909        - **interaction_map_dir (str)**:<br />
1910            The directory where the computed interaction maps will be saved.
1911
1912        - **nproc (int)**:<br />
1913            The number of processes to use for parallel computation of the maps.
1914
1915        - **overwrite (bool, optional):**:<br />
1916            Whether to overwrite existing map files in the interaction_map_dir. If False,
1917            the function will load existing maps from disk if they are available, and skip
1918            recomputation. Note that the plots are always overwritten to reflect the current
1919            binarization settings, but the raw maps are not recomputed if the files already exist.
1920
1921        - **binarize_dmap (bool, optional):**:<br />
1922            Whether to binarize the distance maps based on the cutoff. If True, the distance
1923            maps will be converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a
1924            contact is defined as present if the distance is less than or equal to the cutoff.
1925            If False, the distance maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values
1926            (e.g. average distances). (default: False)
1927
1928        - **binarize_cmap (bool, optional):**:<br />
1929            Whether to binarize the contact maps based on the cutoff. If True, the contact maps
1930            will be converted to binary maps using the `get_binary_map` function, where a contact
1931            is defined as present if the contact frequency is greater than or equal to the cutoff.
1932            If False, the contact maps will not be binarized and will retain their original values
1933            (e.g. average contact frequencies). (default: False)
1934        """
1935        (
1936            pairwise_dmaps,
1937            pairwise_cmaps
1938        ) = self.pairwise_maps_handler.fetch_pairwise_maps(
1939            interaction_map_dir=interaction_map_dir,
1940            nproc=nproc,
1941            overwrite=overwrite,
1942        )
1943
1944        self.pairwise_dmaps = self.pairwise_maps_handler.process_pairwise_maps(
1945            pairwise_maps=pairwise_dmaps,
1946            map_type="dmap",
1947            merge_operation="average",
1948            merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1949            binarize_map=binarize_dmap,
1950        )
1951
1952        self.pairwise_cmaps = self.pairwise_maps_handler.process_pairwise_maps(
1953            pairwise_maps=pairwise_cmaps,
1954            map_type="cmap",
1955            merge_operation="max",
1956            merge_copies=self.merge_copies,
1957            binarize_map=binarize_cmap,
1958        )
1959
1960        if self.merge_copies:
1961            self.xyzr_parser.merge_residue_selection_by_copies()
1962            self.molwise_residues = self.xyzr_parser.molwise_residues
1963
1964        self.map_slices = self.generate_map_slices(
1965            pairwise_keys=list(self.pairwise_dmaps.keys()),
1966        )

def generate_map_slices(self, pairwise_keys: list) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]]: 
1989    def generate_map_slices(
1990        self,
1991        pairwise_keys: list,
1992    ) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]]:
1993        """ Generate a dictionary of slice names and their corresponding residue
1994        ranges for each molecule pair.
1995
1996        ## Arguments:
1997
1998        - **pairwise_keys (list)**:<br />
1999            A list of molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") corresponding to the
2000            keys in the pairwise_maps dictionary. This is used to ensure that the
2001            generated slice names are consistent with the keys in the pairwise_maps
2002            dictionary, and to filter out any selected molecule pairs that do not have
2003            corresponding maps.
2004
2005        ## Returns:
2006
2007        - **dict**:<br />
2008            A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to dictionaries of slice names and
2009            their corresponding residue ranges. Format:
2010            {
2011                "MOL1:MOL2": {
2012                    "slice_name1": {
2013                        "s1": start residue number for mol1,
2014                        "e1": end residue number for mol1,
2015                        "s2": start residue number for mol2,
2016                        "e2": end residue number for mol2,
2017                    },
2018                    "slice_name2": {
2019                        ...
2020                    },
2021                    ...
2022                },
2023                ...
2024            }
2025        """
2026
2027        map_slices = {k: {} for k in pairwise_keys}
2028
2029        for _m1, _m2 in self.sel_mol_pairs:
2030
2031            _base1, _cp_idx1, sel1 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m1).groups()
2032            _base2, _cp_idx2, sel2 = re.match(REGEX_MOLNAME, _m2).groups()
2033
2034            mol1 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m1, only_base=self.merge_copies)
2035            mol2 = XYZRParser.get_mol_name(_m2, only_base=self.merge_copies)
2036
2037            range1 = f"{min(self.molwise_residues[mol1])}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{max(self.molwise_residues[mol1])}"
2038            range2 = f"{min(self.molwise_residues[mol2])}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{max(self.molwise_residues[mol2])}"
2039
2040            pair_name = (
2041                f"{mol1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range1}" +
2042                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2043                f"{mol2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{range2}"
2044            )
2045
2046            if pair_name not in pairwise_keys:
2047                print(f"Warning: {pair_name} not found in computed maps. Skipping.")
2048                continue
2049
2050            s1, e1 = get_res_range_from_key(sel1)[0], get_res_range_from_key(sel1)[-1]
2051            s2, e2 = get_res_range_from_key(sel2)[0], get_res_range_from_key(sel2)[-1]
2052
2053            slice_name = (
2054                f"{mol1}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{s1}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{e1}" +
2055                f"{PAIR_SEP}" +
2056                f"{mol2}{MOL_RANGE_SEP}{s2}{RES_RANGE_SEP}{e2}"
2057            )
2058
2059            map_slices[pair_name][slice_name] = {
2060                "s1": int(s1),
2061                "e1": int(e1),
2062                "s2": int(s2),
2063                "e2": int(e2),
2064            }
2065
2066        return map_slices

Generate a dictionary of slice names and their corresponding residue ranges for each molecule pair.

Arguments:

  • pairwise_keys (list):
    A list of molecule pair names (e.g. "MOL1:MOL2") corresponding to the keys in the pairwise_maps dictionary. This is used to ensure that the generated slice names are consistent with the keys in the pairwise_maps dictionary, and to filter out any selected molecule pairs that do not have corresponding maps.

Returns:

  • dict:
    A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to dictionaries of slice names and their corresponding residue ranges. Format: { "MOL1:MOL2": { "slice_name1": { "s1": start residue number for mol1, "e1": end residue number for mol1, "s2": start residue number for mol2, "e2": end residue number for mol2, }, "slice_name2": { ... }, ... }, ... }

2114
2115        - **plotting_lib (str, optional):**:<br />
2116            The plotting library to use for generating the plots. Can be either
2117            "matplotlib" or "plotly". Default is "matplotlib".
2118        """
2119
2120        output_types = output_type.split("+")
2121        assert all([ot in ["patches", "plots"] for ot in output_types]), (
2122            f"Invalid output_type: {output_type}. Expected 'patches', 'plots', or 'patches+plots'."
2123        )
2124        nproc = min(nproc, len(pairwise_maps), 20)
2125        executor = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=nproc)
2126
2127        if "plots" in output_types:
2128            for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
2129                executor.submit(
2130                    Interaction.plot_map,
2131                    pairwise_maps[pair_name],
2132                    pair_name,
2133                    interaction_map_dir,
2134                    map_type,
2135                    cutoff,
2136                    self.molwise_residues,
2137                    self.map_slices[pair_name],
2138                    plotting_lib,
2139                    binarize_map,
2140                )
2141
2142        if "patches" in output_types:
2143            if not binarize_map:
2144                pairwise_maps = {
2145                    pair_name: get_binary_map(
2146                        q_map=pairwise_maps[pair_name].astype(self.f_dtype),
2147                        binarization_cutoff=cutoff,
2148                        map_type=map_type,
2149                        i_dtype=self.i_dtype,
2150                    )
2151                    for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys()
2152                }
2153
2154            for pair_name in pairwise_maps.keys():
2155
2156                executor.submit(
2157                    Interaction.matrix_patches_worker,
2158                    pairwise_maps[pair_name].astype(self.i_dtype),
2159                    pair_name,
2160                    interaction_map_dir,
2161                )
2162
2163        executor.shutdown(wait=False)
2164        print(f"Saved {map_type} maps and plots to {interaction_map_dir}")

Save the processed interaction maps as plots and/or patches.

Arguments:

  • pairwise_maps (_type_):
    A dictionary mapping molecule pair names to their corresponding distance or contact maps (numpy arrays).

  • interaction_map_dir (_type_):
    The directory where the output maps and plots will be saved.

  • nproc (_type_):
    The number of processes to use for parallel processing when saving the maps and plots.

  • cutoff (_type_):
    The cutoff distance used for binarization of the maps, which will be included in the plot title and colorbar label. See get_binary_map() for more details.

  • binarize_map (_type_):
    Whether to binarize the maps before saving and plotting. If True, the maps will be converted to binary maps based on the cutoff value before saving and plotting.

  • map_type (_type_):
    A string indicating the type of maps being saved and plotted. Should be either "dmap" for distance maps or "cmap" for contact maps.

  • output_type (str, optional)::
    A string indicating the type of output to save. Can be either "patches", "plots", or "patches+plots".

    • If "patches", only the patches will be saved as csv files.
    • If "plots", only the plots will be saved as png files.
    • If "patches+plots", both the patches and plots will be saved.

  • plotting_lib (str, optional)::
    The plotting library to use for generating the plots. Can be either "matplotlib" or "plotly". Default is "matplotlib".
